entries.title: Panache static methods bypass CDI @Alternative stores — returns empty results silently
entries.body:
Panache static methods bypass CDI @Alternative stores — returns empty results silently

## Panache static methods bypass CDI @Alternative stores — returns empty results silently

### Symptom

Test suite activates `@Alternative @Priority(1)` InMemory stores via `quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives`. Panache static queries (`Entity.<Entity>listAll()`, `Entity.find(...)`) return zero results with no error, even though data was inserted through the store.

### Root cause

Panache static methods resolve directly against JPA at the persistence layer, bypassing CDI entirely. `@Alternative` implementations intercept calls made through injected CDI interfaces, not through static Panache entry points. With InMemory stores active, the JPA entity tables are empty — Panache statics query empty tables and return zero results silently.

### Fix

In test code that activates InMemory stores, never use Panache statics to query domain entities. Always go through the injected store or service layer:

```java
// Wrong — bypasses CDI alternative, queries empty JPA table
List<Channel> channels = Channel.<Channel>listAll();

// Correct — routes through the injected alternative store
List<Channel> channels = channelStore.findAll();
// or via service/tool layer
var result = tools.listChannels();
```

### Why this is non-obvious

Panache statics look like repository methods and feel like they should respect CDI alternatives — but they don't. No error is thrown, no warning is logged; the query simply returns an empty collection. The only signal is silently wrong test data.

**See also:** [GE-20260429-a79d0e](GE-20260429-a79d0e.md) — @Alternative @Priority auto-activates without quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives

**See also:** [GE-20260519-f33c66](GE-20260519-f33c66.md) — 'Reactive' service classes may use Panache statics internally — CDI @Alternative doesn't intercept

**See also:** [GE-20260528-3d3847](GE-20260528-3d3847.md) — @Transactional on @BeforeAll static methods has no effect (same CDI proxy limitation)

**See also:** [GE-20260608-d223af](GE-20260608-d223af.md) — REST Assured GPath $.findAll returns null (not []) — Hamcrest not(empty()) silently passes on null

**See also:** [GE-20260609-49bd08](GE-20260609-49bd08.md) — static Panache entity calls bypass injected store tenant filtering

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
Panache static methods alternative store zero results
CDI @Alternative intercepting Panache static queries
InMemory store test fails Panache listAll returns empty

entries.title: @Alternative @Priority(1) from an external JAR does not override a non-alternative bean in Quarkus — needs exclude-types + selected-alternatives
entries.body:
@Alternative @Priority(1) from an external JAR does not override a non-alternative bean in Quarkus — needs exclude-types + selected-alternatives

## Symptom

Test assertions calling `workItemStore.scanAll()` return empty even though the handler log confirms `WorkItemService.create()` ran successfully. `planItem.getStatus()` is `RUNNING` (proving the handler completed), but the store shows nothing.

## Context

Two `WorkItemStore` beans on the test classpath:
- `JpaWorkItemStore @ApplicationScoped` — production bean from `casehub-work`
- `InMemoryWorkItemStore @Alternative @Priority(1)` — test replacement from `casehub-work-testing`

CDI 4.x spec says `@Priority` on an alternative activates it globally and it should win over non-alternatives. In Quarkus ARC 3.32.2 this does not hold when the alternative comes from an external dependency JAR.

## What was tried

- Adding `InMemoryWorkItemStore` to `quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives` alone → "Ambiguous dependencies" deployment failure (both beans active simultaneously)
- `quarkus.arc.exclude-types=io.casehub.work.runtime.repository.jpa.JpaWorkItemStore` alone → no effect; `JpaWorkItemStore` still wins
- `@Inject InMemoryWorkItemStore workItemStore` (concrete type) in the test → bypasses CDI alternative selection; test clears the right store but `WorkItemService` still writes to JPA (H2), so `scanAll()` returns empty

## Root Cause

`@Alternative @Priority(1)` from a dependency JAR is not treated as overriding a non-alternative `@ApplicationScoped` bean by Quarkus ARC. CDI spec §2.6.2 requires `@Priority` alternatives to take precedence, but ARC's resolution appears to treat both as equally active candidates when neither is the local application class. The non-alternative wins or ambiguity is raised.

## Fix

Combine both in `src/test/resources/application.properties`:

```properties
# Remove the JPA impl from CDI discovery entirely
quarkus.arc.exclude-types=io.casehub.work.runtime.repository.jpa.JpaWorkItemStore

# Explicitly select the in-memory replacement
quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives=\
  io.casehub.work.testing.InMemoryWorkItemStore,\
  ...other alternatives...
```

With `JpaWorkItemStore` excluded, `InMemoryWorkItemStore` is the only active `WorkItemStore` bean. Explicit `selected-alternatives` listing then activates it. Both `WorkItemService` (via `@Inject WorkItemStore`) and the test (via `@Inject InMemoryWorkItemStore`) now reference the same singleton, and `scanAll()` finds what `create()` stored.

## Why this is non-obvious

CDI 4.x spec (and Quarkus docs on alternatives) state that `@Alternative @Priority(n)` globally activates and prioritises the alternative. A developer familiar with CDI 4.x would expect `@Priority(1)` to simply work. The failure is silent — no warning is emitted, `JpaWorkItemStore` just wins quietly. The symptom (empty `scanAll()`) points toward a different root cause (session caching, test isolation) and sends debugging in the wrong direction.

**See also:** [GE-20260429-a79d0e](GE-20260429-a79d0e.md) — @Alternative @Priority auto-activates within same module | [GE-20260521-4de4f1](GE-20260521-4de4f1.md) — TestProfile.getEnabledAlternatives() replaces selected-alternatives entirely

**See also:** [GE-20260601-cee623](GE-20260601-cee623.md) — QuarkusTestProfile.getEnabledAlternatives() replaces selected-alternatives entirely

**See also:** [GE-20260601-848232](GE-20260601-848232.md) — exclude-types silently does nothing for beans from Jandex-indexed JARs

**See also:** [GE-20260604-2f0889](GE-20260604-2f0889.md) — @Alternative @Priority(N) stubs appear in @All List<T> alongside original bean

**See also:** [GE-20260616-d70e7e](GE-20260616-d70e7e.md) — selected-alternatives silently accepts non-@Alternative beans

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
@Alternative @Priority(1) ambiguity Quarkus
exclude-types JpaWorkItemStore
selected-alternatives InMemoryWorkItemStore

entries.title: Quarkus ARC @DefaultBean injection points resolve before @Alternative activation in external JARs
entries.body:
Quarkus ARC @DefaultBean injection points resolve before @Alternative activation in external JARs

### Symptom

A `@DefaultBean` reactive bridge (`BlockingToReactiveCbrBridge`) that injects a blocking SPI interface (`CbrCaseMemoryStore`) silently resolves to the no-op `@DefaultBean` implementation (`NoOpCbrCaseMemoryStore`) instead of the `@Alternative @Priority(2)` in-memory implementation (`InMemoryCbrCaseMemoryStore`), even when:

- The alternative is listed in `quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives`
- Both JARs are indexed via `quarkus.index-dependency`
- Direct injection of the blocking interface in a test class correctly resolves to the alternative

The retrieval returns empty with no error or warning — completely silent.

### Context

This occurs when three beans implement the same interface across two external JARs:

- **JAR A** (`casehub-neocortex-memory`): `NoOpCbrCaseMemoryStore` (`@DefaultBean @ApplicationScoped`) and `BlockingToReactiveCbrBridge` (`@DefaultBean @ApplicationScoped`, injects `CbrCaseMemoryStore`)
- **JAR B** (`casehub-neocortex-memory-cbr-inmem`): `InMemoryCbrCaseMemoryStore` (`@Alternative @Priority(2) @ApplicationScoped`)

The bridge in JAR A is supposed to delegate to whichever `CbrCaseMemoryStore` is active. When `InMemoryCbrCaseMemoryStore` is activated via `selected-alternatives`, direct injection works — but the bridge's own injection point does not.

### What was tried (didn't work)

1. Adding `quarkus.index-dependency` for both JARs — no effect on resolution
2. Adding `InMemoryCbrCaseMemoryStore` to `quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives` in the memory profile — direct injection works, bridge delegation does not
3. Adding `quarkus.arc.exclude-types` for `NoOpCbrCaseMemoryStore` — breaks CDI wiring entirely (the bridge has no delegate)

### Root cause

Quarkus ARC resolves `@DefaultBean` beans' injection points at build time. When the bridge (`@DefaultBean`) is being wired, ARC resolves its `@Inject CbrCaseMemoryStore` using the standard `@DefaultBean` resolution rules — which picks the other `@DefaultBean` (`NoOpCbrCaseMemoryStore`) in the same JAR. The `@Alternative` from the external JAR is not considered for the bridge's injection point even though it would be selected for direct injection sites.

Confirmed via `System.identityHashCode()` tracing: both the test's `@Inject CbrCaseMemoryStore` and the bridge's `@Inject CbrCaseMemoryStore delegate` resolve to the same `NoOpCbrCaseMemoryStore_ClientProxy` instance.

### Solution 1 — Bypass the reactive bridge

**Approach:** Inject the blocking interface directly and offload to a worker thread.

**Pros:** No CDI resolution ambiguity. Works with any test profile.

**Cons:** Caller must handle thread offloading explicitly.

```java
@ApplicationScoped
public class MyService {
    @Inject CbrCaseMemoryStore cbrStore; // blocking, not reactive

public Uni<List<Result>> retrieve(Query query) {
        return Uni.createFrom()
            .item(() -> cbrStore.retrieveSimilar(query, MyCase.class))
            .runSubscriptionOn(Infrastructure.getDefaultWorkerPool())
            .map(this::mapResults);
    }
}
```

### Solution 2 — Use QuarkusTestProfile.getEnabledAlternatives()

**Approach:** Override alternatives programmatically in the test profile.

**Pros:** Properly activates @Alternative beans for all injection points including bridge delegates.

**Cons:** `getEnabledAlternatives()` REPLACES (not appends to) `quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives` — ALL alternatives from the base profile must be re-declared. Missing one breaks other tests sharing the profile.

```java
public static class MemoryProfile implements QuarkusTestProfile {
    @Override
    public String getConfigProfile() { return "memory"; }

@Override
    public Set<Class<?>> getEnabledAlternatives() {
        return Set.of(
            InMemoryCaseMetaModelRepository.class,
            InMemoryReactiveCaseMetaModelRepository.class,
            // ... ALL other memory profile alternatives ...
            InMemoryCbrCaseMemoryStore.class);
    }
}
```

### Why this is non-obvious

The bridge pattern (`@DefaultBean` reactive wrapper delegating to `@DefaultBean` blocking implementation, replaced by `@Alternative` at test time) is a standard Quarkus CDI pattern. Nothing in Quarkus documentation warns that `@DefaultBean` injection points resolve before `@Alternative` activation. The failure is completely silent — no ambiguity error, no warning, just empty results from the no-op. Only `System.identityHashCode()` tracing reveals which implementation was actually injected.

### Why this fix

Solution 1 (bypass the bridge) is preferred because it eliminates the CDI resolution issue entirely and has no test infrastructure side effects. Solution 2 works but creates a maintenance burden — every new alternative added to the memory profile must also be added to every `getEnabledAlternatives()` override.

### Alternatives considered

- `quarkus.arc.exclude-types` for the no-op: breaks CDI wiring when the bridge needs a delegate and no alternative is available
- Using `Instance<CbrCaseMemoryStore>` with programmatic lookup: adds complexity without addressing the root cause
- Filing a Quarkus ARC bug: may be working as designed (build-time CDI optimisation)

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
`NoOpCbrCaseMemoryStore`
`@Alternative @Priority(2)` resolution
`quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives`

entries.title: QuarkusTestProfile.getEnabledAlternatives() replaces quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives — does not merge
quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives default priority 1 creates tie with @Priority(1) subclass beans — two @ApplicationScoped instances with separate state
entries.body:
quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives default priority 1 creates tie with @Priority(1) subclass beans — two @ApplicationScoped instances with separate state

### Symptom
`CaseInstance not found or wrong tenant` (or similar state-not-found error) despite the instance being saved moments earlier. The save and lookup use the same `CaseInstanceRepository` interface, but they resolve to different `@ApplicationScoped` bean instances with separate `ConcurrentHashMap` stores.

### Context
`casehub-engine-testing` provides `TestCaseInstanceRepository extends InMemoryCaseInstanceRepository` with `@Alternative @Priority(1) @ApplicationScoped`. This is the standard test harness — it auto-activates without `selected-alternatives`.

A consumer project adds `InMemoryCaseInstanceRepository` to `quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives` in test `application.properties`, thinking it's redundant but harmless.

### What was tried (didn't work)
- Checking event bus threading and Vert.x serialization — object identity was intact
- Verifying `currentPrincipal.tenancyId()` consistency — MockCurrentPrincipal returns a constant
- Adding more beans to `selected-alternatives` — made it worse

### Root cause
Quarkus Arc assigns a **default priority of 1** to alternatives listed in `quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives` that don't have `@Priority`. This creates a priority tie:

- `InMemoryCaseInstanceRepository` — priority 1 (from `selected-alternatives` default)
- `TestCaseInstanceRepository` — priority 1 (from `@Priority(1)`)

Both are `@ApplicationScoped`, so CDI creates **two separate bean instances**. Each has its own `ConcurrentHashMap<UUID, CaseInstance> store`. If CDI resolves different injection points to different beans (or resolves non-deterministically), saves go to one store and lookups to another.

### Fix
Do not add parent classes to `selected-alternatives` when the engine-testing module already provides `@Priority(1)` subclasses:

```properties
# WRONG — creates priority tie with TestCaseInstanceRepository
quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives=...,io.casehub.persistence.memory.InMemoryCaseInstanceRepository

# RIGHT — let engine-testing's @Priority(1) beans handle it
quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives=...
# (omit InMemoryCaseInstanceRepository, InMemoryCaseMetaModelRepository, InMemoryEventLogRepository)
```

The engine-testing module exists specifically to provide auto-activating alternatives for test contexts. Adding the parent classes to `selected-alternatives` defeats the purpose.

### Why this is non-obvious
Adding a class to `selected-alternatives` feels like an explicit, high-confidence activation — surely it would "win" over a `@Priority(1)` subclass. But the default priority is also 1, creating an exact tie. The Quarkus docs mention the default priority but don't warn about ties with existing `@Priority(1)` alternatives on the classpath. The symptom (state not found) appears as a threading or serialization bug, not a CDI resolution issue.

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
`CaseInstance not found or wrong tenant` error
`quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives priority tie`
`ConcurrentHashMap store`

entries.title: quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives in application.properties activates @Alternative beans in @QuarkusTest — beans.xml is ignored
entries.body:
quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives in application.properties activates @Alternative beans in @QuarkusTest — beans.xml is ignored

## What it is

`quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives` in `application.properties` (or test `application.properties`) is the correct way to activate `@Alternative` CDI beans in a Quarkus application — including in `@QuarkusTest` contexts.

```properties
# In src/test/resources/application.properties or src/main/resources/application.properties
quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives=com.example.MyAlternativeRepository
```

Multiple alternatives can be comma-separated.

## Why it's undocumented / non-obvious

The standard CDI mechanism for activating alternatives is `beans.xml`:
```xml
<beans>
  <alternatives>
    <class>com.example.MyAlternativeRepository</class>
  </alternatives>
</beans>
```

In Quarkus with Arc (the CDI implementation), **`beans.xml` alternative activation is silently ignored at build time**. Arc processes CDI at build time and does not honour the `beans.xml` `<alternatives>` section. There is no warning, no error — the `@Alternative` bean is simply not activated, and the original bean (or no bean) is used instead. This causes `UnsatisfiedResolutionException` at startup if nothing else provides the bean.

The `quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives` property is the Quarkus-specific replacement but is not prominently documented alongside the `@Alternative` annotation documentation.

## Context

Common scenario: a Quarkus extension provides an `@Alternative @ApplicationScoped` repository bean (e.g. `JpaLedgerEntryRepository`) that yields to consumer-provided implementations in production. In `@QuarkusTest` integration tests, you want to activate the base implementation since no consumer repo exists in the test module.

## Fix

Add to `src/test/resources/application.properties`:

```properties
quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives=io.example.JpaLedgerEntryRepository
```

Do NOT add `<alternatives>` to `beans.xml` — it will have no effect in Quarkus Arc.

## Why this is non-obvious

The CDI spec says `beans.xml` alternatives work. Quarkus Arc silently diverges from this for build-time optimization reasons. The property name `selected-alternatives` is not listed in the CDI or Arc extension documentation alongside `@Alternative` — it requires reading the Arc configuration reference which is separate from the CDI programming model docs.

## Update — test-local classes in src/test/java need no quarkus.index-dependency

When the `@Alternative` class lives in a **external jar** (a separate Maven module), you must tell Quarkus to index it:

```properties
quarkus.index-dependency.mymodule.group-id=io.example
quarkus.index-dependency.mymodule.artifact-id=my-alternatives-module
```

However, if the `@Alternative` class lives directly in `src/test/java/` of the same module, **no `quarkus.index-dependency` is needed**. Quarkus automatically indexes the test source root for `@QuarkusTest`. Only classes in external jars require the explicit index-dependency config.

```properties
# This is sufficient when @Alternative classes are in src/test/java/:
quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives=io.example.InMemoryRepository

# quarkus.index-dependency is NOT needed — test sources are auto-indexed
```

This is useful when avoiding Maven module cycles: copy the alternative implementations into the module's own `src/test/java/` and the `selected-alternatives` property works without any additional indexing configuration.

## Update — @Alternative @IfBuildProperty beans also need selected-alternatives (not just @QuarkusTest)

When `@Alternative` is combined with `@IfBuildProperty`, the bean is registered at build time when the property matches, but **registration alone does not make it the active CDI alternative**. The `@Alternative` selection still requires `quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives`, even in production `application.properties`.

This surfaces when activating a Quarkus extension's reactive stack via a build property. For example, Qhorus's reactive services are `@Alternative @IfBuildProperty(name = "quarkus.datasource.qhorus.reactive", stringValue = "true") @ApplicationScoped`. Setting the property in `application.properties` registers the beans at augmentation but they still do not win CDI resolution without explicit selection:

```properties
# application.properties — both properties are required to activate reactive Qhorus beans
quarkus.datasource.qhorus.reactive=true
quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives=\
  io.casehub.qhorus.runtime.channel.ReactiveChannelService,\
  io.casehub.qhorus.runtime.message.ReactiveMessageService,\
  ...
```

**The @Priority workaround:** If the bean is annotated `@Alternative @Priority(N)`, Arc selects it automatically without `selected-alternatives`. The `@Priority` annotation is the preferred mechanism for extension-provided alternatives that should activate without consumer configuration. For consumer-configured beans, `selected-alternatives` remains the explicit control point.

## Update — selected-alternatives is build-time: %test. profile prefix has no effect

`quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives` is evaluated during Quarkus augmentation (build time), not at runtime. Profile prefixes like `%test.` are resolved at runtime and therefore **have no effect** on this property.

This means you must write:
```properties
# CORRECT — no profile prefix; the property applies globally at augmentation
quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives=io.casehub.persistence.memory.MemorySubCaseGroupRepository
```

Not:
```properties
# WRONG — %test. is silently ignored for build-time properties; the alternative is not activated
%test.quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives=io.casehub.persistence.memory.MemorySubCaseGroupRepository
```

entries.title: casehub-qhorus MessageService methods using Panache static calls bypass InMemory store in @QuarkusTest
Hibernate dirty-check flushes PanacheEntity field writes inside Panache.withSession() — even for in-memory test stores
entries.body:
Hibernate dirty-check flushes PanacheEntity field writes inside Panache.withSession() — even for in-memory test stores

### Symptom
A JPA UPDATE fires for a field write on a `PanacheEntity` subclass, even though:
- The CDI injection test confirms the in-memory store (`InMemoryReactiveChannelStore`) is selected, not the JPA store
- The entity was created with `new Channel()` — never explicitly `persist()`ed or loaded in the current session
- `quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives` is correctly configured

Error:
```
org.hibernate.QueryParameterException: No argument for named parameter ':tenancyId'
```

### Context
`ReactiveMessageService.dispatch()` wraps the entire dispatch in `Panache.withSession("qhorus", () -> ...)`. Inside that session scope, the in-memory store's `updateLastActivity()` does:

```java
channel.lastActivityAt = Instant.now();
```

`Channel` is a Hibernate-enhanced `PanacheEntity`. The field write is intercepted by Hibernate's dirty tracker within the active session scope and generates a JPA UPDATE at session flush.

### Root cause
Hibernate's bytecode enhancement instruments all `PanacheEntity` subclasses with dirty tracking. Any field write on an enhanced entity within an active `Panache.withSession()` scope is detected and queued for flush — regardless of whether the entity was explicitly persisted or loaded in that session. The CDI injection test proves the right bean is injected, but it does not reveal that Hibernate's session-scoped dirty tracker is intercepting field mutations on enhanced entities.

### Fix
Make the in-memory store's `updateLastActivity()` a no-op. Do not modify enhanced entity fields in-place within a `withSession()` scope:

```java
@Override
public Uni<Void> updateLastActivity(UUID channelId, String tenancyId) {
    // No-op — modifying the Hibernate-enhanced entity in-place triggers
    // a dirty-check flush when called from within Panache.withSession().
    return Uni.createFrom().voidItem();
}
```

`lastActivityAt` is set at channel creation time via `put()`; staleness tracking is irrelevant in test contexts.

### Why this is non-obvious
The CDI direct injection test is a convincing false positive: `@Inject ReactiveChannelStore` returns `InMemoryReactiveChannelStore` ✅. This proves the right bean is injected, but it does not prove that field mutations on Hibernate-enhanced entities are safe within the dispatch session scope. The JPA UPDATE is generated by Hibernate's session-level flush mechanism, not by the in-memory store calling `repo.update()` directly.

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
PanacheEntity dirty-check flush
Hibernate session scope dirty tracker
quarkus arc panache withSession

entries.title: 'Reactive' Quarkus service classes may use blocking services or Panache statics internally — CDI @Alternative in-memory stores don't intercept those paths
entries.body:
'Reactive' Quarkus service classes may use blocking services or Panache statics internally — CDI @Alternative in-memory stores don't intercept those paths

### What is undocumented

A service class annotated `@Alternative` and named with "Reactive" may internally use a `blockingService` field (injected blocking CDI service) for write operations and `Entity.find()` (a Panache static) for read operations. CDI `@Alternative @Priority(1)` in-memory stores only intercept at CDI injection points — Panache statics go directly to the underlying database regardless of what alternatives are selected.

### Context

In Quarkus Qhorus (casehubio/qhorus), `ReactiveQhorusMcpTools`:
- `sendMessage()` delegates internally to `blockingMessageService` → `MessageService.send()` → `messageStore.put()` (uses the `MessageStore` CDI alternative, i.e. `InMemoryMessageStore` in tests)
- `getChannelTimeline()` delegates to `blockingGetChannelTimeline()` → `Message.<Message>find(...)` (Panache static — queries H2 directly, bypasses `MessageStore` entirely)

Result: messages written by `sendMessage()` land in `InMemoryMessageStore` (in-memory). Messages read by `getChannelTimeline()` come from H2 (empty in tests). The two paths never share data.

### Discovery

Only visible by reading the service implementation source. The class name and method signatures suggest a uniform reactive abstraction. Not mentioned in any documentation.

### Impact on tests

Tests that call `sendMessage()` then verify the timeline via `getChannelTimeline()` always see an empty timeline in test setups using `@Alternative` in-memory stores, even though the message was "successfully" posted.

### Fix / Workaround

Identify the actual data path for each operation you need to test:
1. Check which CDI service field the MCP tool method delegates to
2. Check whether that service uses CDI store injection or Panache statics
3. For end-to-end write→read tests: use the real H2 database (don't rely on in-memory stores for both sides)

Alternatively, file an upstream issue to make the read path use the same abstraction as the write path.

**See also:** [GE-20260512-66d997](GE-20260512-66d997.md) — Panache static methods bypass CDI @Alternative stores

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
What is undocumented about Reactive Quarkus service classes?
How do Panache statics bypass CDI @Alternative in-memory stores?
Why do messages written by sendMessage() not land in the InMemoryMessageStore?

entries.title: quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives silently ignores %dev. profile overrides — use exclude-types instead
entries.body:
quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives silently ignores %dev. profile overrides — use exclude-types instead

### Symptom
`%dev.quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives` is set in `application.properties` alongside a non-profiled `quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives`. In dev mode, the `@Alternative` beans listed in the `%dev.` value are never activated — ArC throws `UnsatisfiedResolutionException` for the interfaces they implement, even though the beans exist on the classpath and have Jandex indices.

### Context
Multi-profile Quarkus application needing different CDI alternatives per environment:
- Production: reactive JPA stores (`engine-persistence-hibernate`)
- Dev mode: in-memory blocking stores (`engine-persistence-memory`)
- Tests: separate `application.properties` with its own `selected-alternatives`

Both `%dev.` and non-profiled values present in the same `application.properties`.

### What was tried (didn't work)
1. `%dev.quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives=MemoryPlanItemStore,...` alongside non-profiled `quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives=JpaPlanItemStore,...` — dev alternatives silently ignored
2. Removing the non-profiled value and using only `%dev.` and `%prod.` — still ignored
3. Verified `%dev.quarkus.arc.exclude-types` DOES work (OidcCurrentPrincipal successfully excluded in dev) — confirms profile overrides work for other ArC properties

### Root cause
`quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives` is a build-time fixed property that does not honour `%profile.` prefixes. The property is resolved once during Quarkus augmentation and profile-specific values are silently discarded. This is not documented — the Quarkus configuration reference does not distinguish which ArC properties support profile overrides.

### Fix
Select ALL alternatives (both JPA and memory) in the non-profiled `selected-alternatives`. Use profile-specific `exclude-types` to control which survive in each environment:

```properties
# Non-profiled: select everything — both JPA and memory alternatives
quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives=\
  io.casehub.persistence.jpa.JpaPlanItemStore,\
  io.casehub.persistence.memory.MemoryPlanItemStore,\
  io.casehub.persistence.memory.InMemoryCaseMetaModelRepository

# Dev: exclude reactive JPA stores → memory stores win
%dev.quarkus.arc.exclude-types=io.casehub.persistence.jpa.JpaPlanItemStore,...

# Prod: exclude memory stores → JPA stores win
%prod.quarkus.arc.exclude-types=io.casehub.persistence.memory.MemoryPlanItemStore,...
```

ArC processes `exclude-types` first (removing beans entirely), then resolves `selected-alternatives` among surviving beans. In each profile, only one alternative per interface survives — no ambiguity.

### Why this is non-obvious
Profile-specific overrides (`%dev.`, `%prod.`) work for most Quarkus properties, including `quarkus.arc.exclude-types`. The natural assumption is that `selected-alternatives` follows the same pattern. There is no error, warning, or log message when the profile override is ignored — the non-profiled value is silently used. The failure manifests as `UnsatisfiedResolutionException` with no hint about profile resolution.

### Why this fix
`exclude-types` is a coarser mechanism (removes the bean entirely vs just not selecting it), but it's the only ArC property that supports profile overrides. The exclude-types-first-then-resolve pattern is architecturally sound: each profile starts from the same selected set and carves out what doesn't belong.

### Alternatives considered
- **Maven profiles** — add/remove JARs per profile. Rejected: adds build complexity and doesn't work with `quarkus:dev` which uses the default Maven profile.
- **`@IfBuildProfile("dev")` wrapper beans** — create dev-only `@ApplicationScoped` beans that delegate to memory stores. Rejected: code duplication across 5+ SPIs, maintenance burden.
- **Separate `application-dev.properties`** — Quarkus doesn't support this pattern (it's a Spring Boot convention).

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives exclude-types
%dev.quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives
UnsatisfiedResolutionException arc

entries.title: CDI @Alternative bypass for quarkus:build: non-@Alternative subclass in app module
entries.body:
CDI @Alternative bypass for quarkus:build: non-@Alternative subclass in app module

## CDI @Alternative bypass for quarkus:build: non-@Alternative subclass in app module

### What

When `quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives` fails to activate `@Alternative` beans during `quarkus:build` (see GE-20260524-2b587e), create a non-`@Alternative @ApplicationScoped` subclass of each needed `@Alternative` bean directly in the application module's own source.

### Why it works

CDI does NOT inherit `@Alternative` from superclasses. A subclass without `@Alternative` is treated as a regular `@Default @ApplicationScoped` bean, satisfying injection points without any `selected-alternatives` configuration. Quarkus always indexes the application module's own source, so the subclass is always discovered — no `quarkus.index-dependency` required.

### Code

For each `@Alternative @ApplicationScoped` SPI implementation in a dependency jar:

```java
// In the application module (src/main/java):
package com.example.app.spi;

import com.lib.InMemoryEventLogRepository;
import jakarta.enterprise.context.ApplicationScoped;

@ApplicationScoped  // no @Alternative — this is @Default
public class AppEventLogRepository extends InMemoryEventLogRepository {}
```

Repeat for each SPI. Inject CDI fields from the parent class are satisfied normally — CDI handles injection into inherited fields when creating the child bean.

### When to use this

- `quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives` isn't activating alternatives during `quarkus:build`
- In-memory/dev implementations needed in production build without real backend (tutorial projects, early-stage dev)
- Want zero `selected-alternatives` configuration while keeping implementation reuse

### Why this is non-obvious

Developers reach for `quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives` (the documented mechanism). When that fails silently, the natural next attempt is compile-scope + index-dependency — which also fails. The subclass approach requires knowing that `@Alternative` is not inherited by subclasses, which is a CDI spec detail most developers haven't needed to rely on.

**See also:** [GE-20260524-2b587e](GE-20260524-2b587e.md) — quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives does not activate @Alternative beans during quarkus:build (the problem this technique solves)

**See also:** [GE-20260427-543663](../quarkus/GE-20260427-543663.md) — @Produces @DefaultBean for library-level overridable CDI defaults

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
What is GE-20260524-2b587e?
How do I bypass `@Alternative` beans in Quarkus builds?
What happens when a non-`@Alternative` subclass is created in the app module?

entries.title: casehub-engine-persistence-memory @Alternative beans need explicit selected-alternatives for SubCaseGroupRepository and PlanItemStore
entries.body:
casehub-engine-persistence-memory @Alternative beans need explicit selected-alternatives for SubCaseGroupRepository and PlanItemStore

### Symptom

Quarkus startup fails with:

```
jakarta.enterprise.inject.spi.DeploymentException: Found 2 deployment problems:
[1] Unsatisfied dependency for type io.casehub.engine.common.spi.SubCaseGroupRepository
    - injection target: SubCaseExecutionHandler constructor
[2] Unsatisfied dependency for type io.casehub.engine.common.spi.SubCaseGroupRepository
    - injection target: SubCaseCompletionService constructor
```

### Context

When a CaseHub harness adds `casehub-engine-blackboard` (required for SubCase lifecycle and M-of-N quorum) alongside `casehub-engine-persistence-memory`, the blackboard beans (`SubCaseExecutionHandler`, `SubCaseCompletionService`) need `SubCaseGroupRepository`. The in-memory implementation (`MemorySubCaseGroupRepository`) exists in persistence-memory but is `@Alternative @ApplicationScoped` — CDI does not activate `@Alternative` beans unless explicitly selected.

The same applies to `MemoryPlanItemStore` and `MemoryReactivePlanItemStore` from the same module.

### What was tried (didn't work)

- Adding Jandex index entries for persistence-memory — beans are discovered but not activated (they're @Alternative)
- Assuming engine-testing would provide @Priority(1) overrides — engine-testing has TestCaseMetaModelRepository, TestCaseInstanceRepository, TestEventLogRepository but NOT TestSubCaseGroupRepository or TestPlanItemStore

### Root cause

`casehub-engine-persistence-memory` ships all repository implementations as `@Alternative @ApplicationScoped` — they require explicit `quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives` to be activated. Engine-testing provides `@Priority(1)` overrides for CaseInstanceRepository and EventLogRepository but not for SubCaseGroupRepository or PlanItemStore.

### Fix

Add to `application.properties` (test or production):

```properties
quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives=\
  io.casehub.persistence.memory.MemorySubCaseGroupRepository,\
  io.casehub.persistence.memory.MemoryPlanItemStore,\
  io.casehub.persistence.memory.MemoryReactivePlanItemStore
```

Append to existing `selected-alternatives` if other beans (e.g. `JpaLedgerEntryRepository`) are already listed.

### Why this is non-obvious

The error names `SubCaseGroupRepository` — but `MemorySubCaseGroupRepository` IS on the classpath and IS Jandex-indexed. The CDI error doesn't mention that the bean exists but is an unselected `@Alternative`. You have to read the source of `MemorySubCaseGroupRepository` to discover the `@Alternative` annotation, then check whether engine-testing provides an override (it doesn't for these SPIs).

## Variant — Runtime failure from implicit activation of remaining @Alternative beans

### Symptom

`@QuarkusTest` starts cleanly (no DeploymentException) because `casehub-engine-testing` provides `@Priority(1)` overrides for `CaseInstanceRepository` and `EventLogRepository`. But the first `startCase()` call in certain test classes fails with:

```
(RECIPIENT_FAILURE,8191) CaseInstance not found or wrong tenant: <uuid>
```

The error comes from `InMemoryCaseInstanceRepository.update()` (persistence-memory) — the bean is implicitly activated by Quarkus Arc as the sole `@Alternative` without a competing non-alternative, but the activation path produces intermittent initialization-order failures.

### Context

When only `SubCaseGroupRepository` and `PlanItemStore` are in `selected-alternatives`, the remaining 4 `@Alternative` beans from persistence-memory rely on Arc's implicit fallback activation:
- `InMemoryCaseInstanceRepository`
- `InMemoryCaseMetaModelRepository`
- `InMemoryEventLogRepository`
- `MemoryReactivePlanItemStore`

This implicit activation works for most test classes but fails intermittently when the test class is among the first to trigger `startCase()` in a fresh JVM — the `CaseStartedEventHandler` calls `caseInstanceRepository.update()` and the instance isn't found.

### Fix

Add all 4 remaining persistence-memory `@Alternative` beans to `selected-alternatives`:

```properties
quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives=\
  ...,\
  io.casehub.persistence.memory.InMemoryCaseInstanceRepository,\
  io.casehub.persistence.memory.InMemoryCaseMetaModelRepository,\
  io.casehub.persistence.memory.InMemoryEventLogRepository,\
  io.casehub.persistence.memory.MemoryReactivePlanItemStore
```

Verified in casehub-aml#58: 4 of 6 failing test classes fixed by explicit selection. 2 remaining failures (`AmlLayer7ResourceTest`, `AmlTrustRoutingAttestationTest`) may have a deeper root cause — investigation ongoing.

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
SubCaseGroupRepository alternative
PlanItemStore alternative
jakarta.enterprise.inject.spi.DeploymentException SubCaseGroupRepository

entries.title: @Alternative @Priority(N) in Quarkus CDI auto-activates without quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives config
quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives does not activate @Alternative beans during quarkus:build
entries.body:
quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives does not activate @Alternative beans during quarkus:build

## quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives does not activate @Alternative beans during quarkus:build

### Symptom

CDI deployment fails with 32 `Unsatisfied dependency` errors for `@Alternative @ApplicationScoped` beans even though they are listed in `quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives` in `application.properties`.

### Context

Quarkus multi-module app with `quarkus:build` in the Maven plugin execution. One or more dependency jars provide `@Alternative @ApplicationScoped` implementations of SPIs. Listing them in `quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives` (with or without `%prod.` profile prefix, with or without multiline backslash continuation) has no effect during production augmentation.

### What was tried (didn't work)

- `quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives=com.example.Foo,com.example.Bar` — no effect
- `%prod.quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives=...` — no effect
- Multiline backslash syntax — no effect
- Adding explicit `quarkus.index-dependency.*` for the jar alongside selected-alternatives — still no effect
- Promoting the dependency from test to compile scope — beans visible to augmentation but still not activated

### Root cause

`quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives` activates alternatives for `@QuarkusTest` augmentation (which reads test-scoped `application.properties`) but NOT during `quarkus:build` (production augmentation). The Quarkus docs describe it as a build-time property, but its activation path for production builds is silently broken or not implemented for dependency jars. Zero documentation of this distinction.

### Fix

Create a non-`@Alternative @ApplicationScoped` subclass of each `@Alternative` bean directly in the application's own source (see GE-20260524-d75218). The subclass inherits the implementation, does NOT inherit `@Alternative`, and is `@Default` — satisfying CDI injection without any `selected-alternatives` configuration.

```java
// In the app module's own source (always indexed by Quarkus):
@ApplicationScoped
public class MyEventLogRepository extends InMemoryEventLogRepository {}
```

### Why this is non-obvious

Quarkus documentation states `quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives` is a build-time property, which implies it applies to all augmentations including production. It works correctly for `@QuarkusTest` but silently fails for `quarkus:build`, with no warning or error about unresolvable alternatives — only a CDI deployment failure with 32+ unsatisfied dependency errors that appear to be unrelated to the activation mechanism.

**See also:** [GE-20260524-d75218](GE-20260524-d75218.md) — CDI @Alternative bypass for quarkus:build: non-@Alternative subclass workaround

**See also:** [GE-20260516-4bf0dc](GE-20260516-4bf0dc.md) — quarkus.arc.exclude-types does not gate JAX-RS @Path resources

**See also:** [GE-20260531-70e07c](GE-20260531-70e07c.md) — Quarkus test-profile arc.exclude-types does not apply to production augmentation

**See also:** [GE-20260601-cee623](GE-20260601-cee623.md) — QuarkusTestProfile.getEnabledAlternatives() replaces selected-alternatives entirely

**See also:** [GE-20260616-d70e7e](GE-20260616-d70e7e.md) — selected-alternatives silently accepts non-@Alternative beans, leaving CDI ambiguity unresolved (a different limitation)

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---

quarkus build alternative bean error
cdi unsatisfied dependency alternative @Alternative

entries.title: @IfBuildProfile + @Alternative + @Priority resolves CDI without selected-alternatives in indexed JARs
entries.body:
@IfBuildProfile + @Alternative + @Priority resolves CDI without selected-alternatives in indexed JARs

### Symptom

Adding a dev-profile-only CDI bean (e.g., a `CurrentPrincipal` for dev mode) via `%dev.quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives=com.example.DevBean` causes startup failures — all beans from the non-profiled `quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives` list disappear.

### Context

Quarkus profile-specific properties (`%dev.`, `%test.`, `%prod.`) completely **replace** their non-profiled counterparts. If the base `application.properties` has:

```properties
quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives=\
  com.example.JpaRepo,\
  com.example.JpaPlanItemStore,\
  com.example.JpaSubCaseGroupRepo
```

Adding `%dev.quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives=com.example.DevBean` drops all three JPA alternatives in dev mode — CDI startup fails with unsatisfied dependency errors for every bean that was in the original list.

### Root cause

Profile-specific properties in Quarkus are full replacements, not merges. This is by design (SmallRye Config behaviour), but the failure mode is silent — no warning that the non-profiled value was dropped.

### Fix

Use bean-level annotations instead of `selected-alternatives`:

```java
@ApplicationScoped
@Alternative
@Priority(150)  // beats OidcCurrentPrincipal @Priority(100)
@IfBuildProfile("dev")
public class DemoCurrentPrincipal implements CurrentPrincipal {
    @Override public String tenancyId() { return "demo-tenant"; }
    @Override public String actorId()   { return "demo-user"; }
}
```

**Requirements:**
1. The bean must live in a **Jandex-indexed JAR** (e.g., the application's own `runtime/` module). ArC discovers it automatically — no `selected-alternatives` entry needed.
2. `@IfBuildProfile("dev")` excludes the bean entirely from non-dev builds — no ambiguity in production.
3. `@Priority(150)` resolves over competing `@Alternative` beans (e.g., `OidcCurrentPrincipal @Priority(100)`) via standard ArC priority resolution.

This is the same mechanism by which `OidcCurrentPrincipal @Alternative @Priority(100)` beats `MockCurrentPrincipal @DefaultBean` in production — without being listed in `selected-alternatives`.

### Why this is non-obvious

The natural instinct is `%dev.quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives=MyDevBean` — it looks like the standard profile-override pattern. The replacement behaviour is documented for SmallRye Config but not prominently flagged in the Quarkus CDI guide. The failure (dropped JPA alternatives) manifests as unrelated `UnsatisfiedResolutionException` errors that don't mention `selected-alternatives` at all.

### Why this fix

`@IfBuildProfile + @Priority` solves the problem at the bean level — no configuration property needed. The alternative (duplicating the full `selected-alternatives` list in every profile override) is fragile and drifts as new alternatives are added.

### Alternatives considered

- **Duplicate the full list in `%dev.`** — works but fragile; every new `@Alternative` bean must be added to every profile-specific override. Drifts silently.
- **Use `@UnlessBuildProfile("prod")` instead of `@IfBuildProfile("dev")`** — activates in both dev and test profiles, which may not be desired. Test profile has its own `FixedCurrentPrincipal @Priority(200)`.

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
quarkus arc selected-alternatives error
cdi startup failure dev profile
@IfBuildProfile alternative priority resolution

entries.title: Quarkus test application.properties replaces selected-alternatives entirely — reactive in-memory repos need explicit activation
entries.body:
Quarkus test application.properties replaces selected-alternatives entirely — reactive in-memory repos need explicit activation

Quarkus test application.properties replaces selected-alternatives entirely — reactive in-memory repos need explicit activation

### Symptom

`quarkus:build` (production CDI validation) fails with `Unsatisfied dependency for type ReactiveCaseInstanceRepository` and similar for `ReactiveEventLogRepository`, `ReactiveSubCaseGroupRepository`. Tests pass because `engine-testing` provides `@Priority(1)` wrappers. The build step validates against main `application.properties` only.

### Context

A dual-stack engine (blocking + reactive SPIs) uses in-memory `@Alternative` implementations for both. Main `application.properties` lists only the blocking repos in `selected-alternatives`. Test `application.properties` lists different alternatives (ledger JPA repos, platform memory stores). `@Priority(1)` Test* wrappers from engine-testing auto-activate in test mode but don't exist on the production classpath.

### Root cause

Quarkus MicroProfile Config resolves `quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives` as a single string property. When test `application.properties` declares the same key, it **replaces** the main value entirely — it does not merge or append. The main properties' blocking repos are no longer activated in test mode, but that's fine because Test* wrappers cover them.

However, `quarkus:build` (invoked by `mvn verify`) validates CDI against the **main** `application.properties`. If the main properties only activate blocking repos, the reactive SPIs are unsatisfied. The reactive in-memory repos (`InMemoryReactiveCaseInstanceRepository`, `InMemoryReactiveEventLogRepository`, etc.) are `@Alternative` without `@Priority` — they need explicit `selected-alternatives` activation.

### Fix

Add all reactive in-memory repo alternatives to the **main** `application.properties`:

```properties
quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives=\
  io.casehub.persistence.memory.MemoryPlanItemStore,\
  io.casehub.persistence.memory.MemoryReactivePlanItemStore,\
  io.casehub.persistence.memory.InMemoryCaseInstanceRepository,\
  io.casehub.persistence.memory.InMemoryReactiveCaseInstanceRepository,\
  io.casehub.persistence.memory.InMemoryEventLogRepository,\
  io.casehub.persistence.memory.InMemoryReactiveEventLogRepository,\
  io.casehub.persistence.memory.InMemoryCaseMetaModelRepository,\
  io.casehub.persistence.memory.InMemoryReactiveCaseMetaModelRepository,\
  io.casehub.persistence.memory.InMemorySubCaseGroupRepository,\
  io.casehub.persistence.memory.InMemoryReactiveSubCaseGroupRepository
```

### Why this is non-obvious

Tests pass — the `@Priority(1)` Test* wrappers handle everything in test mode. The failure only appears during `quarkus:build`, which runs CDI validation against the main properties. The error messages name reactive SPI interfaces that the developer never directly uses, making it unclear which concrete beans to activate.

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---

`Unsatisfied dependency` reactive SPIs

entries.title: Panache static methods bypass CDI @Alternative stores — returns empty results silently
entries.body:
Panache static methods bypass CDI @Alternative stores — returns empty results silently

## Panache static methods bypass CDI @Alternative stores — returns empty results silently

### Symptom

Test suite activates `@Alternative @Priority(1)` InMemory stores via `quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives`. Panache static queries (`Entity.<Entity>listAll()`, `Entity.find(...)`) return zero results with no error, even though data was inserted through the store.

### Root cause

Panache static methods resolve directly against JPA at the persistence layer, bypassing CDI entirely. `@Alternative` implementations intercept calls made through injected CDI interfaces, not through static Panache entry points. With InMemory stores active, the JPA entity tables are empty — Panache statics query empty tables and return zero results silently.

### Fix

In test code that activates InMemory stores, never use Panache statics to query domain entities. Always go through the injected store or service layer:

```java
// Wrong — bypasses CDI alternative, queries empty JPA table
List<Channel> channels = Channel.<Channel>listAll();

// Correct — routes through the injected alternative store
List<Channel> channels = channelStore.findAll();
// or via service/tool layer
var result = tools.listChannels();
```

### Why this is non-obvious

Panache statics look like repository methods and feel like they should respect CDI alternatives — but they don't. No error is thrown, no warning is logged; the query simply returns an empty collection. The only signal is silently wrong test data.

**See also:** [GE-20260429-a79d0e](GE-20260429-a79d0e.md) — @Alternative @Priority auto-activates without quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives

**See also:** [GE-20260519-f33c66](GE-20260519-f33c66.md) — 'Reactive' service classes may use Panache statics internally — CDI @Alternative doesn't intercept

**See also:** [GE-20260528-3d3847](GE-20260528-3d3847.md) — @Transactional on @BeforeAll static methods has no effect (same CDI proxy limitation)

**See also:** [GE-20260608-d223af](GE-20260608-d223af.md) — REST Assured GPath $.findAll returns null (not []) — Hamcrest not(empty()) silently passes on null

**See also:** [GE-20260609-49bd08](GE-20260609-49bd08.md) — static Panache entity calls bypass injected store tenant filtering

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
Panache static methods alternative store zero results
CDI @Alternative intercepting Panache static queries
InMemory store test fails Panache listAll returns empty

entries.title: Quarkus augmentation demands datasource for extension-registered JPA entities even when in-memory CDI alternatives handle persistence
entries.body:
Quarkus augmentation demands datasource for extension-registered JPA entities even when in-memory CDI alternatives handle persistence

### Symptom

Test module depends on a Quarkus extension (e.g. `casehub-ledger`) whose runtime JAR contains `@Entity` classes. The test classpath includes an in-memory persistence module with `@Alternative @Priority(1)` implementations that bypass JPA entirely. Despite this, Quarkus startup fails:

```
ConfigurationException: Persistence unit '<default>' defines entities
[io.casehub.ledger.runtime.model.ActorIdentity, ...] but its datasource
'<default>' cannot be found: Datasource '<default>' is not configured.
```

### Context

The test module's `pom.xml` depends on the Quarkus extension runtime and an in-memory persistence module. No datasource is configured because the in-memory implementations handle all reads/writes via `ConcurrentHashMap` — JPA is never used at runtime.

### What was tried (didn't work)

Running tests with only the in-memory persistence module on the classpath and no datasource configuration. Expected the `@Alternative @Priority(1)` in-memory implementations to eliminate the need for any JPA/datasource setup.

### Root cause

Quarkus augmentation discovers `@Entity` classes via Jandex index scanning of extension runtime JARs. `HibernateOrmProcessor#configurationDescriptorBuilding` validates that every persistence unit with discovered entities has a configured datasource. This validation runs at **build time** — before CDI bean resolution. `@Alternative @Priority(1)` annotations are CDI concepts resolved at **runtime**. Augmentation has no visibility into which CDI alternatives will replace which beans.

The mental model "in-memory alternatives replace JPA" is correct at runtime but wrong at augmentation time.

### Fix

Add `quarkus-jdbc-h2` as a test dependency and configure a minimal H2 datasource in `application.properties`:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
  <artifactId>quarkus-jdbc-h2</artifactId>
  <scope>test</scope>
</dependency>
```

```properties
quarkus.datasource.db-kind=h2
quarkus.datasource.jdbc.url=jdbc:h2:mem:testdb;MODE=PostgreSQL;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1
quarkus.datasource.username=sa
quarkus.datasource.password=

quarkus.hibernate-orm.database.generation=none
quarkus.flyway.migrate-at-start=true
quarkus.flyway.locations=classpath:db/ledger/migration
```

The datasource satisfies augmentation validation. The in-memory `@Alternative @Priority(1)` implementations still handle all actual persistence at runtime — H2 is never queried.

### Why this is non-obvious

The `@Alternative @Priority(1)` pattern is specifically designed to replace default implementations. A developer correctly reasons: "I'm replacing all JPA repositories with in-memory alternatives, so I don't need a datasource." This reasoning is valid at the CDI layer but fails because Quarkus augmentation validates the JPA layer independently, before CDI alternatives are resolved.

### Why this fix

The H2 datasource is a no-op cost — it exists only to satisfy augmentation. The alternative (`quarkus.hibernate-orm.enabled=false`) would disable the entire Hibernate subsystem, which may break other extension features that rely on entity metadata even when in-memory persistence handles the actual data.

### Alternatives considered

- `quarkus.hibernate-orm.enabled=false` — disables Hibernate entirely; rejected because extension deployment processors may rely on entity metadata for build-time validation or code generation
- Excluding entity classes from Jandex — not feasible; the entities are in the extension JAR which is already indexed

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
`Quarkus augmentation datasource entity error`
`Jandex index processing HibernateOrmProcessor`
`CDI alternative persistence unit conflict`

entries.title: @Alternative @Priority(1) from an external JAR does not override a non-alternative bean in Quarkus — needs exclude-types + selected-alternatives
entries.body:
@Alternative @Priority(1) from an external JAR does not override a non-alternative bean in Quarkus — needs exclude-types + selected-alternatives

## Symptom

Test assertions calling `workItemStore.scanAll()` return empty even though the handler log confirms `WorkItemService.create()` ran successfully. `planItem.getStatus()` is `RUNNING` (proving the handler completed), but the store shows nothing.

## Context

Two `WorkItemStore` beans on the test classpath:
- `JpaWorkItemStore @ApplicationScoped` — production bean from `casehub-work`
- `InMemoryWorkItemStore @Alternative @Priority(1)` — test replacement from `casehub-work-testing`

CDI 4.x spec says `@Priority` on an alternative activates it globally and it should win over non-alternatives. In Quarkus ARC 3.32.2 this does not hold when the alternative comes from an external dependency JAR.

## What was tried

- Adding `InMemoryWorkItemStore` to `quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives` alone → "Ambiguous dependencies" deployment failure (both beans active simultaneously)
- `quarkus.arc.exclude-types=io.casehub.work.runtime.repository.jpa.JpaWorkItemStore` alone → no effect; `JpaWorkItemStore` still wins
- `@Inject InMemoryWorkItemStore workItemStore` (concrete type) in the test → bypasses CDI alternative selection; test clears the right store but `WorkItemService` still writes to JPA (H2), so `scanAll()` returns empty

## Root Cause

`@Alternative @Priority(1)` from a dependency JAR is not treated as overriding a non-alternative `@ApplicationScoped` bean by Quarkus ARC. CDI spec §2.6.2 requires `@Priority` alternatives to take precedence, but ARC's resolution appears to treat both as equally active candidates when neither is the local application class. The non-alternative wins or ambiguity is raised.

## Fix

Combine both in `src/test/resources/application.properties`:

```properties
# Remove the JPA impl from CDI discovery entirely
quarkus.arc.exclude-types=io.casehub.work.runtime.repository.jpa.JpaWorkItemStore

# Explicitly select the in-memory replacement
quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives=\
  io.casehub.work.testing.InMemoryWorkItemStore,\
  ...other alternatives...
```

With `JpaWorkItemStore` excluded, `InMemoryWorkItemStore` is the only active `WorkItemStore` bean. Explicit `selected-alternatives` listing then activates it. Both `WorkItemService` (via `@Inject WorkItemStore`) and the test (via `@Inject InMemoryWorkItemStore`) now reference the same singleton, and `scanAll()` finds what `create()` stored.

## Why this is non-obvious

CDI 4.x spec (and Quarkus docs on alternatives) state that `@Alternative @Priority(n)` globally activates and prioritises the alternative. A developer familiar with CDI 4.x would expect `@Priority(1)` to simply work. The failure is silent — no warning is emitted, `JpaWorkItemStore` just wins quietly. The symptom (empty `scanAll()`) points toward a different root cause (session caching, test isolation) and sends debugging in the wrong direction.

**See also:** [GE-20260429-a79d0e](GE-20260429-a79d0e.md) — @Alternative @Priority auto-activates within same module | [GE-20260521-4de4f1](GE-20260521-4de4f1.md) — TestProfile.getEnabledAlternatives() replaces selected-alternatives entirely

**See also:** [GE-20260601-cee623](GE-20260601-cee623.md) — QuarkusTestProfile.getEnabledAlternatives() replaces selected-alternatives entirely

**See also:** [GE-20260601-848232](GE-20260601-848232.md) — exclude-types silently does nothing for beans from Jandex-indexed JARs

**See also:** [GE-20260604-2f0889](GE-20260604-2f0889.md) — @Alternative @Priority(N) stubs appear in @All List<T> alongside original bean

**See also:** [GE-20260616-d70e7e](GE-20260616-d70e7e.md) — selected-alternatives silently accepts non-@Alternative beans

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
@Alternative @Priority(1) ambiguity Quarkus
exclude-types JpaWorkItemStore
selected-alternatives InMemoryWorkItemStore

entries.title: 'Reactive' Quarkus service classes may use blocking services or Panache statics internally — CDI @Alternative in-memory stores don't intercept those paths
entries.body:
'Reactive' Quarkus service classes may use blocking services or Panache statics internally — CDI @Alternative in-memory stores don't intercept those paths

### What is undocumented

A service class annotated `@Alternative` and named with "Reactive" may internally use a `blockingService` field (injected blocking CDI service) for write operations and `Entity.find()` (a Panache static) for read operations. CDI `@Alternative @Priority(1)` in-memory stores only intercept at CDI injection points — Panache statics go directly to the underlying database regardless of what alternatives are selected.

### Context

In Quarkus Qhorus (casehubio/qhorus), `ReactiveQhorusMcpTools`:
- `sendMessage()` delegates internally to `blockingMessageService` → `MessageService.send()` → `messageStore.put()` (uses the `MessageStore` CDI alternative, i.e. `InMemoryMessageStore` in tests)
- `getChannelTimeline()` delegates to `blockingGetChannelTimeline()` → `Message.<Message>find(...)` (Panache static — queries H2 directly, bypasses `MessageStore` entirely)

Result: messages written by `sendMessage()` land in `InMemoryMessageStore` (in-memory). Messages read by `getChannelTimeline()` come from H2 (empty in tests). The two paths never share data.

### Discovery

Only visible by reading the service implementation source. The class name and method signatures suggest a uniform reactive abstraction. Not mentioned in any documentation.

### Impact on tests

Tests that call `sendMessage()` then verify the timeline via `getChannelTimeline()` always see an empty timeline in test setups using `@Alternative` in-memory stores, even though the message was "successfully" posted.

### Fix / Workaround

Identify the actual data path for each operation you need to test:
1. Check which CDI service field the MCP tool method delegates to
2. Check whether that service uses CDI store injection or Panache statics
3. For end-to-end write→read tests: use the real H2 database (don't rely on in-memory stores for both sides)

Alternatively, file an upstream issue to make the read path use the same abstraction as the write path.

**See also:** [GE-20260512-66d997](GE-20260512-66d997.md) — Panache static methods bypass CDI @Alternative stores

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
What is undocumented about Reactive Quarkus service classes?
How do Panache statics bypass CDI @Alternative in-memory stores?
Why do messages written by sendMessage() not land in the InMemoryMessageStore?

Quarkus ARC @Alternative @Priority(1) subclass not injected when injection point uses concrete superclass type
entries.body:
Quarkus ARC @Alternative @Priority(1) subclass not injected when injection point uses concrete superclass type

### Symptom
Consumer `@QuarkusTest` integration tests fail with `CaseInstance not found or wrong tenant` — 34 of 228 tests. The reactive repository and blocking repository maintain separate in-memory stores despite both being `@ApplicationScoped` singletons.

### Context
Dual-stack persistence pattern: blocking repo is canonical, reactive repo delegates to it via `@Inject`. Both have `@Alternative` test wrappers with `@Priority(1)` in an `engine-testing` module.

### What was tried (didn't work)
- Checked all event bus handlers for tenant context propagation — all correct
- Checked `CurrentPrincipal` thread safety — `@ApplicationScoped`, consistent
- Traced `save()` → `update()` flow — tenancyId parameters matched
- Assumed CDI would resolve `@Inject InMemoryCaseInstanceRepository delegate` to `TestCaseInstanceRepository extends InMemoryCaseInstanceRepository` via assignability

### Root cause
`InMemoryReactiveCaseInstanceRepository` declared its delegate as:
```java
@Inject InMemoryCaseInstanceRepository delegate;  // concrete class
```
`TestCaseInstanceRepository extends InMemoryCaseInstanceRepository` with `@Alternative @Priority(1)` was NOT substituted as the delegate. ARC resolved the injection point to a separate `InMemoryCaseInstanceRepository` instance — creating two stores with independent state.

### Fix
Inject by SPI interface instead of concrete class:
```java
@Inject CaseInstanceRepository delegate;  // SPI interface
```
ARC correctly resolves `@Alternative @Priority(1)` candidates when the injection point is the interface type. Applied to all 5 reactive in-memory repos.

### Why this is non-obvious
CDI spec says `@Alternative` beans are eligible for any injection point they satisfy by type. The expectation is that `TestCaseInstanceRepository extends InMemoryCaseInstanceRepository` satisfies `@Inject InMemoryCaseInstanceRepository`. The failure is silent — no CDI ambiguity error, no deployment failure. Two separate bean instances are created, and the symptom (tenant mismatch) gives no hint about the CDI root cause.

### Alternatives considered
- Making `TestCaseInstanceRepository` a `@Specializes` bean — rejected: Quarkus ARC has limited `@Specializes` support
- Using `@Produces` method to bridge — rejected: adds unnecessary complexity when interface injection works

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
`Quarkus ARC injection delegate`
`ARC @Alternative substitution`
`CaseInstanceRepository SPI inject`

quarkus-hibernate-reactive-panache in an extension forces Hibernate Reactive to boot for all consumers — @Alternative does not prevent it
entries.body:
quarkus-hibernate-reactive-panache in an extension forces Hibernate Reactive to boot for all consumers — @Alternative does not prevent it

## quarkus-hibernate-reactive-panache in an extension forces Hibernate Reactive to boot for all consumers — @Alternative does not prevent it

**ID:** GE-20260420-dcec35
**Stack:** Quarkus 3.32.2, quarkus-hibernate-reactive-panache

**Symptom:** Adding `quarkus-hibernate-reactive-panache` to a Quarkus extension's runtime `pom.xml` causes `FastBootHibernateReactivePersistenceProvider` to try to initialise on every consumer app startup — even those with no reactive datasource configured. Error: `Unable to find datasource '<default>' for persistence unit '<default>': No pool has been defined`.

Three test classes fail that previously passed: the two using `@TestProfile` (which restart Quarkus) and the one with `@TestTransaction` that triggers JTA coordination with all registered persistence units.

### Root cause
The Hibernate Reactive Panache extension scans for `PanacheRepositoryBase` implementations at **build time** (AOT). Any class implementing the interface — even an `@Alternative` bean — causes the extension to register a reactive persistence unit for the associated entity. `@Alternative` suppresses CDI bean activation but does NOT suppress the build-step registration. At runtime, Hibernate Reactive tries to find a reactive (Vert.x) pool for the registered persistence unit and fails if none is configured.

### Fix
Add to the consumer's test `application.properties`:

```properties
quarkus.datasource.reactive=false
```

This prevents Hibernate Reactive from claiming a reactive pool at runtime, even though the persistence unit was registered at build time.

### Why non-obvious
The error message points to a missing datasource pool — suggesting the fix is to configure a datasource, not to disable reactive. Marking the `PanacheRepositoryBase` bean as `@Alternative` is the obvious CDI workaround and feels correct, but `@Alternative` only controls CDI injection — it has no effect on Quarkus build steps. The fix (`quarkus.datasource.reactive=false`) suppresses the runtime pool lookup entirely, not via CDI.

### Alternatives considered
- `@Alternative` on reactive beans — does not prevent build-step registration; persistence unit still created
- `quarkus.hibernate-reactive.active=false` — property not recognised in Quarkus 3.32.2
- Testcontainers + PostgreSQL — works but adds heavy test infrastructure; unnecessary when H2 suffices

**See also:** GE-20260420-45d53b (fix: quarkus.datasource.reactive=false), GE-20260420-daf5dc (optional dep variant of same issue)

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---

hibernate reactive persistence provider initialization

entries.title: Hibernate dirty-check flushes PanacheEntity field writes inside Panache.withSession() — even for in-memory test stores
entries.body:
Hibernate dirty-check flushes PanacheEntity field writes inside Panache.withSession() — even for in-memory test stores

### Symptom
A JPA UPDATE fires for a field write on a `PanacheEntity` subclass, even though:
- The CDI injection test confirms the in-memory store (`InMemoryReactiveChannelStore`) is selected, not the JPA store
- The entity was created with `new Channel()` — never explicitly `persist()`ed or loaded in the current session
- `quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives` is correctly configured

Error:
```
org.hibernate.QueryParameterException: No argument for named parameter ':tenancyId'
```

### Context
`ReactiveMessageService.dispatch()` wraps the entire dispatch in `Panache.withSession("qhorus", () -> ...)`. Inside that session scope, the in-memory store's `updateLastActivity()` does:

```java
channel.lastActivityAt = Instant.now();
```

`Channel` is a Hibernate-enhanced `PanacheEntity`. The field write is intercepted by Hibernate's dirty tracker within the active session scope and generates a JPA UPDATE at session flush.

### Root cause
Hibernate's bytecode enhancement instruments all `PanacheEntity` subclasses with dirty tracking. Any field write on an enhanced entity within an active `Panache.withSession()` scope is detected and queued for flush — regardless of whether the entity was explicitly persisted or loaded in that session. The CDI injection test proves the right bean is injected, but it does not reveal that Hibernate's session-scoped dirty tracker is intercepting field mutations on enhanced entities.

### Fix
Make the in-memory store's `updateLastActivity()` a no-op. Do not modify enhanced entity fields in-place within a `withSession()` scope:

```java
@Override
public Uni<Void> updateLastActivity(UUID channelId, String tenancyId) {
    // No-op — modifying the Hibernate-enhanced entity in-place triggers
    // a dirty-check flush when called from within Panache.withSession().
    return Uni.createFrom().voidItem();
}
```

`lastActivityAt` is set at channel creation time via `put()`; staleness tracking is irrelevant in test contexts.

### Why this is non-obvious
The CDI direct injection test is a convincing false positive: `@Inject ReactiveChannelStore` returns `InMemoryReactiveChannelStore` ✅. This proves the right bean is injected, but it does not prove that field mutations on Hibernate-enhanced entities are safe within the dispatch session scope. The JPA UPDATE is generated by Hibernate's session-level flush mechanism, not by the in-memory store calling `repo.update()` directly.

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
PanacheEntity dirty-check flush
Hibernate session scope dirty tracker
quarkus arc panache withSession

entries.title: casehub-engine-persistence-memory @Alternative beans need explicit selected-alternatives for SubCaseGroupRepository and PlanItemStore
entries.body:
casehub-engine-persistence-memory @Alternative beans need explicit selected-alternatives for SubCaseGroupRepository and PlanItemStore

### Symptom

Quarkus startup fails with:

```
jakarta.enterprise.inject.spi.DeploymentException: Found 2 deployment problems:
[1] Unsatisfied dependency for type io.casehub.engine.common.spi.SubCaseGroupRepository
    - injection target: SubCaseExecutionHandler constructor
[2] Unsatisfied dependency for type io.casehub.engine.common.spi.SubCaseGroupRepository
    - injection target: SubCaseCompletionService constructor
```

### Context

When a CaseHub harness adds `casehub-engine-blackboard` (required for SubCase lifecycle and M-of-N quorum) alongside `casehub-engine-persistence-memory`, the blackboard beans (`SubCaseExecutionHandler`, `SubCaseCompletionService`) need `SubCaseGroupRepository`. The in-memory implementation (`MemorySubCaseGroupRepository`) exists in persistence-memory but is `@Alternative @ApplicationScoped` — CDI does not activate `@Alternative` beans unless explicitly selected.

The same applies to `MemoryPlanItemStore` and `MemoryReactivePlanItemStore` from the same module.

### What was tried (didn't work)

- Adding Jandex index entries for persistence-memory — beans are discovered but not activated (they're @Alternative)
- Assuming engine-testing would provide @Priority(1) overrides — engine-testing has TestCaseMetaModelRepository, TestCaseInstanceRepository, TestEventLogRepository but NOT TestSubCaseGroupRepository or TestPlanItemStore

### Root cause

`casehub-engine-persistence-memory` ships all repository implementations as `@Alternative @ApplicationScoped` — they require explicit `quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives` to be activated. Engine-testing provides `@Priority(1)` overrides for CaseInstanceRepository and EventLogRepository but not for SubCaseGroupRepository or PlanItemStore.

### Fix

Add to `application.properties` (test or production):

```properties
quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives=\
  io.casehub.persistence.memory.MemorySubCaseGroupRepository,\
  io.casehub.persistence.memory.MemoryPlanItemStore,\
  io.casehub.persistence.memory.MemoryReactivePlanItemStore
```

Append to existing `selected-alternatives` if other beans (e.g. `JpaLedgerEntryRepository`) are already listed.

### Why this is non-obvious

The error names `SubCaseGroupRepository` — but `MemorySubCaseGroupRepository` IS on the classpath and IS Jandex-indexed. The CDI error doesn't mention that the bean exists but is an unselected `@Alternative`. You have to read the source of `MemorySubCaseGroupRepository` to discover the `@Alternative` annotation, then check whether engine-testing provides an override (it doesn't for these SPIs).

## Variant — Runtime failure from implicit activation of remaining @Alternative beans

### Symptom

`@QuarkusTest` starts cleanly (no DeploymentException) because `casehub-engine-testing` provides `@Priority(1)` overrides for `CaseInstanceRepository` and `EventLogRepository`. But the first `startCase()` call in certain test classes fails with:

```
(RECIPIENT_FAILURE,8191) CaseInstance not found or wrong tenant: <uuid>
```

The error comes from `InMemoryCaseInstanceRepository.update()` (persistence-memory) — the bean is implicitly activated by Quarkus Arc as the sole `@Alternative` without a competing non-alternative, but the activation path produces intermittent initialization-order failures.

### Context

When only `SubCaseGroupRepository` and `PlanItemStore` are in `selected-alternatives`, the remaining 4 `@Alternative` beans from persistence-memory rely on Arc's implicit fallback activation:
- `InMemoryCaseInstanceRepository`
- `InMemoryCaseMetaModelRepository`
- `InMemoryEventLogRepository`
- `MemoryReactivePlanItemStore`

This implicit activation works for most test classes but fails intermittently when the test class is among the first to trigger `startCase()` in a fresh JVM — the `CaseStartedEventHandler` calls `caseInstanceRepository.update()` and the instance isn't found.

### Fix

Add all 4 remaining persistence-memory `@Alternative` beans to `selected-alternatives`:

```properties
quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives=\
  ...,\
  io.casehub.persistence.memory.InMemoryCaseInstanceRepository,\
  io.casehub.persistence.memory.InMemoryCaseMetaModelRepository,\
  io.casehub.persistence.memory.InMemoryEventLogRepository,\
  io.casehub.persistence.memory.MemoryReactivePlanItemStore
```

Verified in casehub-aml#58: 4 of 6 failing test classes fixed by explicit selection. 2 remaining failures (`AmlLayer7ResourceTest`, `AmlTrustRoutingAttestationTest`) may have a deeper root cause — investigation ongoing.

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
SubCaseGroupRepository alternative
PlanItemStore alternative
jakarta.enterprise.inject.spi.DeploymentException SubCaseGroupRepository

entries.title: @Alternative @Priority(1) beans in a test-helper jar are invisible to downstream @QuarkusTest — no Jandex index
entries.body:
@Alternative @Priority(1) beans in a test-helper jar are invisible to downstream @QuarkusTest — no Jandex index

## Context

Building a `casehub-testing` module to provide `@Alternative @Priority(1)` in-memory repository implementations that downstream `@QuarkusTest` classes can consume by just adding the module as a test dependency — no `quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives` config needed.

## Symptom

```
jakarta.enterprise.inject.UnsatisfiedResolutionException: Unsatisfied dependency
  for type io.casehub.engine.spi.CaseInstanceRepository and qualifiers [@Default]
```

Downstream `@QuarkusTest` fails to start even though `casehub-testing` is on the classpath and its `TestCaseInstanceRepository` carries `@Alternative @Priority(1) @ApplicationScoped`.

## Root Cause

Quarkus CDI bean discovery requires a Jandex index to scan beans from classpath JARs. If the testing helper JAR does not build a Jandex index (i.e., the `jandex-maven-plugin` or equivalent is not configured), Quarkus cannot see any of its beans — including `@Alternative @Priority(1)` classes. The annotation is present in the bytecode but the JAR is effectively invisible to CDI.

The `casehub-testing` pom.xml had no Jandex configuration, so its beans were never indexed.

## Fix

**Option A (recommended for reusable testing jars):** Add Jandex indexing to the helper module's pom.xml:

```xml
<plugin>
    <groupId>io.smallrye</groupId>
    <artifactId>jandex-maven-plugin</artifactId>
    <executions>
        <execution>
            <id>make-index</id>
            <goals><goal>jandex</goal></goals>
        </execution>
    </executions>
</plugin>
```

**Option B (proven fallback):** Keep in-memory implementations in `casehub-persistence-memory` without `@Priority`, and activate them via `quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives` in `src/test/resources/application.properties`:

```properties
quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives=\
  io.casehub.persistence.memory.InMemoryCaseInstanceRepository,\
  io.casehub.persistence.memory.InMemoryCaseMetaModelRepository,\
  io.casehub.persistence.memory.InMemoryEventLogRepository
```

Option B is what every other module in the project already uses and is the safe, proven path.

## Why This Is Non-Obvious

The `@Alternative @Priority(1)` pattern is supposed to be self-activating — you expect it to "just work" when the JAR is on the classpath. The failure message says "unsatisfied dependency" which points to a missing implementation, not to a missing index. Nothing in the error or Quarkus startup log mentions Jandex.

**See also:** [GE-20260423-a01832](GE-20260423-a01832.md) — @Alternative beans in third-party test jars not scanned without explicit index config | [GE-20260421-03fa72](GE-20260421-03fa72.md) — optional module jar missing Jandex index | [GE-20260417-c59817](GE-20260417-c59817.md) — quarkus.arc.selected-alternatives activates @Alternative beans | [GE-20260427-62d3ab](GE-20260427-62d3ab.md) — @Alternative @Priority(1) inner beans as test spies | [GE-20260424-59906a](GE-20260424-59906a.md) — CDI does not scan @ApplicationScoped beans in plain JAR module | [GE-0133](GE-0133.md) — CDI silently ignores beans in jars without Jandex index

**See also:** GE-20260422-ebb91d — CDI AmbiguousResolutionException when multiple @ApplicationScoped beans implement the same SPI interface
**See also:** [GE-20260415-884e48 — @Alternative @Priority(n) in CDI 4.0/Quarkus globally activates the alternative — causes AmbiguousResolutionException](GE-20260415-884e48.md)

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
