entries.title: Quarkus Hibernate Reactive @QuarkusTest cannot use H2 — vertx-jdbc-client alone doesn't register the reactive pool factory
entries.body:
Quarkus Hibernate Reactive @QuarkusTest cannot use H2 — vertx-jdbc-client alone doesn't register the reactive pool factory

## Symptom

`@QuarkusTest` with `quarkus.datasource.reactive=true` (set via `@TestProfile`) and `vertx-jdbc-client` on the classpath fails at context startup:

```
No reactive datasource configured
```

or the reactive Hibernate session is never initialised and all `@RunOnVertxContext` tests are skipped/fail. Adding `quarkus.datasource.reactive.url=h2:mem:...` doesn't help.

## Root Cause

Quarkus's reactive pool factory is only registered by **native reactive client Quarkus extensions** — `quarkus-reactive-pg-client`, `quarkus-reactive-mysql-client`, etc. The raw `vertx-jdbc-client` jar is a JDBC bridge, but Quarkus does not wire it as a managed reactive datasource. H2 has no native async driver; there is no Quarkus reactive H2 extension.

## Fix

For reactive Hibernate Panache integration tests, use PostgreSQL with Docker:

1. Add `quarkus-reactive-pg-client` as a test dependency
2. Enable Dev Services (requires Docker): Quarkus auto-starts a PostgreSQL container
3. Set `quarkus.datasource.reactive=true` and `quarkus.datasource.db-kind=postgresql` in the test profile

If Docker is unavailable, write the reactive JPA tests as `@Disabled` with an explanatory comment. Unit tests via `InMemoryReactive*Store` (direct instantiation, `.await().indefinitely()`) still work without any datasource.

## Why This Is Non-Obvious

`vertx-jdbc-client` is described as a JDBC bridge that enables reactive-style access over blocking JDBC drivers. It's reasonable to assume adding it to the classpath would enable reactive H2. The Quarkus docs don't document this limitation explicitly — the reactive datasource section discusses PostgreSQL, MySQL, and MariaDB but doesn't mention that other drivers simply won't work regardless of the JDBC bridge.

**See also:** GE-20260416-f02f95 (VertxContextSupport.subscribeAndAwait() for reactive Panache in tests), GE-20260420-33b95f (H2 + hibernate-reactive classpath fix)

**See also:** GE-20260420-daf5dc (optional dep still activates Hibernate Reactive extension)

**See also:** [GE-20260508-492336](../casehub-qhorus/GE-20260508-492336.md) — casehub-qhorus activates quarkus-hibernate-reactive unconditionally, fails with JDBC H2

entries.title: Hibernate @PreUpdate fires at flush time, not at persist() — denormalized fields are stale in the returned object
Quarkus augmentation demands datasource for extension-registered JPA entities even when in-memory CDI alternatives handle persistence
entries.body:
Quarkus augmentation demands datasource for extension-registered JPA entities even when in-memory CDI alternatives handle persistence

### Symptom

Test module depends on a Quarkus extension (e.g. `casehub-ledger`) whose runtime JAR contains `@Entity` classes. The test classpath includes an in-memory persistence module with `@Alternative @Priority(1)` implementations that bypass JPA entirely. Despite this, Quarkus startup fails:

```
ConfigurationException: Persistence unit '<default>' defines entities
[io.casehub.ledger.runtime.model.ActorIdentity, ...] but its datasource
'<default>' cannot be found: Datasource '<default>' is not configured.
```

### Context

The test module's `pom.xml` depends on the Quarkus extension runtime and an in-memory persistence module. No datasource is configured because the in-memory implementations handle all reads/writes via `ConcurrentHashMap` — JPA is never used at runtime.

### What was tried (didn't work)

Running tests with only the in-memory persistence module on the classpath and no datasource configuration. Expected the `@Alternative @Priority(1)` in-memory implementations to eliminate the need for any JPA/datasource setup.

### Root cause

Quarkus augmentation discovers `@Entity` classes via Jandex index scanning of extension runtime JARs. `HibernateOrmProcessor#configurationDescriptorBuilding` validates that every persistence unit with discovered entities has a configured datasource. This validation runs at **build time** — before CDI bean resolution. `@Alternative @Priority(1)` annotations are CDI concepts resolved at **runtime**. Augmentation has no visibility into which CDI alternatives will replace which beans.

The mental model "in-memory alternatives replace JPA" is correct at runtime but wrong at augmentation time.

### Fix

Add `quarkus-jdbc-h2` as a test dependency and configure a minimal H2 datasource in `application.properties`:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
  <artifactId>quarkus-jdbc-h2</artifactId>
  <scope>test</scope>
</dependency>
```

```properties
quarkus.datasource.db-kind=h2
quarkus.datasource.jdbc.url=jdbc:h2:mem:testdb;MODE=PostgreSQL;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1
quarkus.datasource.username=sa
quarkus.datasource.password=

quarkus.hibernate-orm.database.generation=none
quarkus.flyway.migrate-at-start=true
quarkus.flyway.locations=classpath:db/ledger/migration
```

The datasource satisfies augmentation validation. The in-memory `@Alternative @Priority(1)` implementations still handle all actual persistence at runtime — H2 is never queried.

### Why this is non-obvious

The `@Alternative @Priority(1)` pattern is specifically designed to replace default implementations. A developer correctly reasons: "I'm replacing all JPA repositories with in-memory alternatives, so I don't need a datasource." This reasoning is valid at the CDI layer but fails because Quarkus augmentation validates the JPA layer independently, before CDI alternatives are resolved.

### Why this fix

The H2 datasource is a no-op cost — it exists only to satisfy augmentation. The alternative (`quarkus.hibernate-orm.enabled=false`) would disable the entire Hibernate subsystem, which may break other extension features that rely on entity metadata even when in-memory persistence handles the actual data.

### Alternatives considered

- `quarkus.hibernate-orm.enabled=false` — disables Hibernate entirely; rejected because extension deployment processors may rely on entity metadata for build-time validation or code generation
- Excluding entity classes from Jandex — not feasible; the entities are in the extension JAR which is already indexed

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
`Quarkus augmentation datasource entity error`
`Jandex index processing HibernateOrmProcessor`
`CDI alternative persistence unit conflict`

entries.title: quarkus-work-core FilterRule JPA entity requires a datasource — modules using in-memory persistence fail startup
entries.body:
quarkus-work-core FilterRule JPA entity requires a datasource — modules using in-memory persistence fail startup

## Symptom

Quarkus startup fails in a module that uses in-memory persistence (no JDBC datasource):

```
ConfigurationException: Datasource '<default>' is not configured.
Persistence unit '<default>' defines entities [io.quarkiverse.work.core.filter.FilterRule],
but its datasource '<default>' cannot be found.
```

## Context

Occurs when `quarkus-work-core` is a transitive dependency (e.g. via `engine` module)
in a Quarkus test module that does not configure a datasource. `FilterRule` is a
`@Entity` (Hibernate ORM Panache) in quarkus-work-core and is discovered by Quarkus's
CDI/Hibernate scanning across all modules on the classpath.

## Root cause

`quarkus-work-core` bundles a `FilterRule` JPA entity and declares Hibernate ORM Panache
as a runtime dependency. Any module that transitively depends on `quarkus-work-core`
inherits the entity scanning, requiring a configured datasource even when the module
has no persistence of its own.

## Fix

Add to the affected module's test `application.properties`:

```properties
# Disable Hibernate ORM so quarkus-work-core's FilterRule entity
# does not require a datasource in modules using in-memory persistence.
quarkus.hibernate-orm.enabled=false
```

## Why this is non-obvious

The module didn't directly depend on `quarkus-work-core` — it arrived as a transitive
dependency through `engine`. The error message names `FilterRule` but gives no indication
of which JAR introduced it or why a datasource is needed in a module that never configured one.

**See also:** GE-20260429-21e6cf "Quarkus: JPA entity in a dependency artifact forces datasource config on ALL downstream consumers"

**See also:** [GE-20260513-74dc72](../casehub-work/GE-20260513-74dc72.md) — casehub-work requires io.casehub.work.runtime.filter in Hibernate scan packages

**See also:** [GE-20260618-08cb96](GE-20260618-08cb96.md) — Named Hibernate ORM PU requires both @PersistenceUnit qualifier AND packages config

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---

entries.title: casehub-qhorus activates quarkus-hibernate-reactive unconditionally — fails with JDBC H2 at startup
entries.body:
casehub-qhorus activates quarkus-hibernate-reactive unconditionally — fails with JDBC H2 at startup

## Symptom

Quarkus fails at startup with an error about a reactive Vert.x pool or reactive datasource not being configured, even though the application only uses JDBC H2 and `casehub.qhorus.reactive.enabled=false` is set.

```
Failed to start quarkus: Reactive datasource 'qhorus' requires a reactive driver
io.quarkus.runtime.QuarkusBindException: ...Vert.x pool...
```

## Context

Any Quarkus application that adds `casehub-qhorus` as a Maven dependency will trigger this failure if it does not provide a reactive datasource. The `casehub.qhorus.reactive.enabled=false` build-time flag exists in qhorus but does **not** suppress the Quarkus hibernate-reactive extension from activating — it only controls qhorus's own reactive messaging layer.

## Root Cause

`casehub-qhorus` has a compile-scope dependency on `quarkus-hibernate-reactive-panache`. When the deployment JAR of that extension is on the classpath, Quarkus activates the reactive persistence layer unconditionally at augmentation time — before any `@IfBuildProperty` guards in qhorus's own processors can suppress it. The result is that Quarkus tries to create a reactive Vert.x pool for every configured datasource, including the default H2 JDBC datasource, which has no reactive driver.

## Fix

Add these properties to `application.properties` (or `src/test/resources/application.properties` for tests):

```properties
# Suppress reactive datasource activation — casehub-qhorus pulls in
# quarkus-hibernate-reactive-panache unconditionally; this prevents Quarkus
# from trying to wire a reactive Vert.x pool to JDBC datasources.
quarkus.datasource.reactive=false
quarkus.datasource.qhorus.reactive=false
```

**Do NOT add `casehub.qhorus.reactive.enabled=false`** — this key was removed from the qhorus config model in a later 0.2-SNAPSHOT build. Adding it now causes `ConfigValidationException` at startup, a hard failure with a misleading error message. The two standard Quarkus properties above are sufficient.

## ⚠️ Deprecated property (added 2026-05-17)

`casehub.qhorus.reactive.enabled=false` was a valid workaround in earlier qhorus 0.2-SNAPSHOT builds but was **removed from the qhorus config model** by qhorus 0.2-SNAPSHOT (circa 2026-05). Adding it to `application.properties` now causes:

```
io.smallrye.config.ConfigValidationException: SRCFG00014: The config property casehub.qhorus.reactive.enabled
with the config value 'false' was converted to null from the converter
```

This is a hard startup failure with a misleading error — it looks like a config parsing problem, not a stale property name. Remove this key from any application.properties file where it was previously added.

## Why This Is Non-Obvious

The error message says "reactive datasource not configured" — pointing at the datasource config, not at qhorus. A developer troubleshooting this naturally adds reactive datasource config rather than suppressing reactive entirely. The qhorus build-time flag (`casehub.qhorus.reactive.enabled`) sounds like it should solve the problem, but it operates at the application layer, not the Quarkus augmentation layer.

### Why this fix

Setting `quarkus.datasource.reactive=false` is the correct Quarkus mechanism to suppress reactive pool creation per datasource. The two-property combination is required because qhorus uses a named datasource (`qhorus`) in addition to the default — both must be suppressed independently.

## Structural Fix

Protocol PP-20260514-f41258 prescribes the correct extension-level fix:
mark `quarkus-hibernate-reactive-panache` as `<optional>true</optional>` in the
runtime pom; in the deployment processor replace the config flag with
`Capabilities.isPresent(Capability.HIBERNATE_REACTIVE)` as the BooleanSupplier;
produce `ExcludedTypeBuildItem` for reactive classes when capability is absent and
for blocking counterparts when it is present. Classpath presence becomes the single
source of truth — no consumer-side suppression needed.

Tracked as casehub-qhorus#141. Once that ships:
- The two-property workaround is obsolete
- Remove reactive suppression from: claudony app/test, devtown app/test, aml app/test, clinical app/test

**See also:** [GE-20260420-cbd0fa](../quarkus/GE-20260420-cbd0fa.md) — Quarkus Hibernate Reactive @QuarkusTest cannot use H2

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
quarkus hibernate-reactive reactive datasource error
casehub-qhorus reactive activation quarkus
quarkus bind exception reactive vertx pool

entries.title: Hibernate 6 SessionFactoryObserverForNamedQueryValidation throws at boot for schema-drifted JARs — quarkus property overrides don't suppress it
entries.body:
Hibernate 6 SessionFactoryObserverForNamedQueryValidation throws at boot for schema-drifted JARs — quarkus property overrides don't suppress it

## Symptom

`@QuarkusTest` fails at boot with:

```
jakarta.persistence.PersistenceException: Unable to build Hibernate SessionFactory
Caused by: org.hibernate.query.NamedQueryValidationException: Errors in named queries:
  Suppressed: org.hibernate.query.sqm.UnknownPathException:
    Could not resolve attribute 'scopeKey' of 'io.casehub.ledger.runtime.model.ActorTrustScore'
```

The error also appears as `ERROR` log lines before the exception:
```
HHH90003001: Error in named query: ActorTrustScore.findGlobalByActorId:
  org.hibernate.query.sqm.UnknownPathException: Could not resolve attribute 'scopeKey'
```

Hibernate throws this at `sessionFactoryCreated()` time — before any test runs.

## Root Cause

A cached `casehub-ledger:0.2-SNAPSHOT` JAR contains `@NamedQuery` annotations on `ActorTrustScore` that reference a field (`scopeKey`) not yet present on the entity class. This happens when the `@NamedQuery` strings were committed to the repo but the corresponding entity field wasn't added yet (or vice versa), and the local Maven cache holds a stale artifact version.

Hibernate 6 validates ALL named queries at `SessionFactory` build time via `SessionFactoryObserverForNamedQueryValidation` — a Quarkus Hibernate ORM extension class. Unlike Hibernate 5, there is no documented configuration key to skip this validation.

**Attempts that don't work:**
- `quarkus.hibernate-orm.validate-named-query=false` — not a valid Quarkus config key
- `quarkus.hibernate-orm.unsupported-properties."hibernate.query.validate_named_queries"=false` — also ineffective; the Quarkus observer runs after Hibernate's own validation hooks

## Fix

Install the affected artifact from local source:

```bash
mvn install -DskipTests -q --batch-mode -f /path/to/ledger/pom.xml
```

This overwrites the stale SNAPSHOT JAR in `~/.m2/` with a consistent version where named queries and entity fields match.

If local source is unavailable, force Maven to re-download the SNAPSHOT:
```bash
mvn dependency:resolve -U  # -U forces SNAPSHOT refresh
```

## Why This Is Non-Obvious

1. The error log says `HHH90003001` and mentions a named query — nothing suggests the problem is a stale JAR artifact. A developer investigates entity mappings, not Maven cache consistency.
2. The entity class on disk is correct; the problem is inside the compiled JAR from cache. Reading source code shows no issue.
3. The two Quarkus/Hibernate property overrides that should disable validation are both silently ignored — the validation happens in a Quarkus extension observer, not in Hibernate's standard configuration layer.
4. Tests pass on CI (which always downloads fresh artifacts) but fail locally on cached SNAPSHOTs — intermittent environment-specific failure with no clear signal.

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
`jakarta.persistence.PersistenceException` `ActorTrustScore`
`SessionFactoryObserverForNamedQueryValidation` `NamedQueryValidationException`
`hibernate.query.sqm.UnknownPathException` `scopeKey`

entries.title: quarkus.datasource.active=false is runtime-only — Hibernate build step still demands a configured datasource
entries.body:
quarkus.datasource.active=false is runtime-only — Hibernate build step still demands a configured datasource

### Symptom
`io.quarkus.runtime.configuration.ConfigurationException: Datasource '<default>' is not configured` at Quarkus augmentation time, despite setting `quarkus.datasource.active=false` and `quarkus.hibernate-orm.active=false` in `application.properties`.

### Context
You have `@Entity` classes on the classpath (from a Quarkus extension runtime module) and want to boot without any real datasource — e.g. using `@Alternative @Priority(100)` in-memory stores that beat the JPA stores. Setting `datasource.active=false` seems like the right approach.

### What was tried (didn't work)
1. `quarkus.datasource.active=false` + `quarkus.hibernate-orm.active=false` — both are runtime properties; the `HibernateOrmProcessor#configurationDescriptorBuilding` build step runs before runtime and demands a datasource when it sees entities.
2. `quarkus.hibernate-orm.enabled=false` — disables entity scanning at build time, but JPA store beans still inject `EntityManager`. With no `EntityManager` bean produced, you get `UnsatisfiedResolutionException`.
3. Excluding JPA stores via `quarkus.arc.exclude-types=io.example.repository.jpa.*` — cascades into `UnsatisfiedResolutionException` for any bean that injects the excluded stores (e.g. a `CrossTenantProducer` that injects `CrossTenantWorkItemStore`). The dependency chain is deeper than the direct excludes.

### Root cause
`quarkus.datasource.active` and `quarkus.hibernate-orm.active` are **runtime** properties — they deactivate beans at runtime but do not affect Quarkus augmentation (build-time). The `HibernateOrmProcessor` build step scans for `@Entity` annotations and validates that a matching datasource exists. This happens before any runtime property is evaluated.

### Fix
Provide a dummy H2 datasource that satisfies build-time validation. Disable Flyway so no migrations run. Let Hibernate generate schema from annotations (never used for actual data):

```properties
quarkus.datasource.db-kind=h2
quarkus.datasource.jdbc.url=jdbc:h2:mem:dummy;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1
quarkus.hibernate-orm.schema-management.strategy=drop-and-create
quarkus.flyway.enabled=false
```

The `@Alternative @Priority(100)` in-memory stores handle all actual persistence. The H2 datasource exists but carries no data.

### Why this is non-obvious
The property name `quarkus.datasource.active=false` strongly implies "don't use a datasource." A developer would reasonably expect it to work at build time. The distinction between build-time augmentation and runtime configuration is not surfaced in the error message — the exception says "Datasource not configured" without mentioning that `active=false` was set and ignored.

### Why this fix
The dummy datasource approach is the only one that avoids cascading CDI failures. Both `hibernate-orm.enabled=false` and `arc.exclude-types` break the CDI wiring graph in ways that require excluding progressively more beans. The dummy datasource keeps the entire CDI graph valid while letting the alternative stores win at runtime.

### Alternatives considered
- **`hibernate-orm.enabled=false`** — rejected because JPA store beans still inject `EntityManager`, which is absent when Hibernate is disabled. Would require all JPA stores to use `@IfBuildProperty` or similar conditional registration.
- **`arc.exclude-types` on JPA packages** — rejected because the dependency chain cascades. Any service bean that injects a store interface (where the only implementation was the excluded JPA store) fails with `UnsatisfiedResolutionException`.
- **No datasource at all** — not possible while `@Entity` classes are on the classpath and the Hibernate extension is present.

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
quarkus hibernate datasource runtime property
hibernate orm processor configuration exception
datasource active false build step

entries.title: Quarkus augmentation demands datasource for extension-registered JPA entities even when in-memory CDI alternatives handle persistence
entries.body:
Quarkus augmentation demands datasource for extension-registered JPA entities even when in-memory CDI alternatives handle persistence

### Symptom

Test module depends on a Quarkus extension (e.g. `casehub-ledger`) whose runtime JAR contains `@Entity` classes. The test classpath includes an in-memory persistence module with `@Alternative @Priority(1)` implementations that bypass JPA entirely. Despite this, Quarkus startup fails:

```
ConfigurationException: Persistence unit '<default>' defines entities
[io.casehub.ledger.runtime.model.ActorIdentity, ...] but its datasource
'<default>' cannot be found: Datasource '<default>' is not configured.
```

### Context

The test module's `pom.xml` depends on the Quarkus extension runtime and an in-memory persistence module. No datasource is configured because the in-memory implementations handle all reads/writes via `ConcurrentHashMap` — JPA is never used at runtime.

### What was tried (didn't work)

Running tests with only the in-memory persistence module on the classpath and no datasource configuration. Expected the `@Alternative @Priority(1)` in-memory implementations to eliminate the need for any JPA/datasource setup.

### Root cause

Quarkus augmentation discovers `@Entity` classes via Jandex index scanning of extension runtime JARs. `HibernateOrmProcessor#configurationDescriptorBuilding` validates that every persistence unit with discovered entities has a configured datasource. This validation runs at **build time** — before CDI bean resolution. `@Alternative @Priority(1)` annotations are CDI concepts resolved at **runtime**. Augmentation has no visibility into which CDI alternatives will replace which beans.

The mental model "in-memory alternatives replace JPA" is correct at runtime but wrong at augmentation time.

### Fix

Add `quarkus-jdbc-h2` as a test dependency and configure a minimal H2 datasource in `application.properties`:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
  <artifactId>quarkus-jdbc-h2</artifactId>
  <scope>test</scope>
</dependency>
```

```properties
quarkus.datasource.db-kind=h2
quarkus.datasource.jdbc.url=jdbc:h2:mem:testdb;MODE=PostgreSQL;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1
quarkus.datasource.username=sa
quarkus.datasource.password=

quarkus.hibernate-orm.database.generation=none
quarkus.flyway.migrate-at-start=true
quarkus.flyway.locations=classpath:db/ledger/migration
```

The datasource satisfies augmentation validation. The in-memory `@Alternative @Priority(1)` implementations still handle all actual persistence at runtime — H2 is never queried.

### Why this is non-obvious

The `@Alternative @Priority(1)` pattern is specifically designed to replace default implementations. A developer correctly reasons: "I'm replacing all JPA repositories with in-memory alternatives, so I don't need a datasource." This reasoning is valid at the CDI layer but fails because Quarkus augmentation validates the JPA layer independently, before CDI alternatives are resolved.

### Why this fix

The H2 datasource is a no-op cost — it exists only to satisfy augmentation. The alternative (`quarkus.hibernate-orm.enabled=false`) would disable the entire Hibernate subsystem, which may break other extension features that rely on entity metadata even when in-memory persistence handles the actual data.

### Alternatives considered

- `quarkus.hibernate-orm.enabled=false` — disables Hibernate entirely; rejected because extension deployment processors may rely on entity metadata for build-time validation or code generation
- Excluding entity classes from Jandex — not feasible; the entities are in the extension JAR which is already indexed

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
`Quarkus augmentation datasource entity error`
`Jandex index processing HibernateOrmProcessor`
`CDI alternative persistence unit conflict`

entries.title: Quarkus: JPA entity in a dependency artifact forces datasource config on ALL downstream consumers
entries.body:
Quarkus: JPA entity in a dependency artifact forces datasource config on ALL downstream consumers

## Symptom

After adding a module that contains JPA `@Entity` classes as a compile dependency, `@QuarkusTest` classes in downstream modules fail at startup with:

```
ConfigurationException: Datasource '<default>' is not configured.
To solve this, configure datasource '<default>'.
```

This happens even if the downstream module uses only in-memory repository implementations and never interacts with the new dependency's entities.

## Context

Triggered when a module (e.g. `quarkus-ledger`) bundles JPA entity classes in its main artifact. Any module that takes this as a compile dependency — even just to use a utility class like `LedgerTraceIdProvider` — inherits all entity classes on its test classpath. Hibernate ORM's Quarkus extension scans ALL entity classes on the classpath and registers them in the default persistence unit. If no datasource is configured, startup fails.

## What was tried

- Setting `quarkus.flyway.migrate-at-start=false` in test `application.properties` — has no effect because `migrate-at-start` is a build-time fixed property baked into the jar's `META-INF/microprofile-config.properties`.
- Setting `quarkus.hibernate-orm.enabled=false` — disables Hibernate ORM entirely, which breaks test discovery for `@QuarkusTest` classes that depend on any ORM-scoped CDI beans.
- `quarkus.arc.exclude-types` to exclude the problematic beans — does not work for extension-registered beans (registered at augmentation time, not CDI discovery time).

## Root Cause

Quarkus scans the full classpath for `@Entity`-annotated classes at build/augmentation time. Any entity class on the classpath — regardless of which module it came from — is registered in the default persistence unit. There is no built-in scoping mechanism to limit entity discovery to a specific module or jar.

The architectural violation is bundling JPA entity classes alongside domain model/SPI code in a single artifact. The correct pattern: keep domain model (plain POJOs) and JPA entities in separate modules.

## Fix

**Short-term (per affected test module):** Add an H2 datasource configuration to the test `application.properties` so Hibernate can start, plus a `NoOpLedgerEntryRepository` stub (or equivalent) as `@Alternative @Priority(1) @ApplicationScoped` to satisfy CDI:

```properties
# application.properties (test)
quarkus.datasource.db-kind=h2
quarkus.datasource.jdbc.url=jdbc:h2:mem:testdb;MODE=PostgreSQL;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1
quarkus.datasource.username=sa
quarkus.datasource.password=
quarkus.hibernate-orm.schema-management.strategy=drop-and-create
quarkus.flyway.migrate-at-start=false
```

```java
@Alternative @Priority(1) @ApplicationScoped
class NoOpLedgerEntryRepository implements LedgerEntryRepository {
  // no-op implementations of all methods
}
```

**Long-term (architectural fix):** Split the offending artifact into:
- `<name>-api` — domain POJOs + SPI interfaces only, zero JPA dependency
- `<name>` or `<name>-hibernate` — JPA entity classes + Flyway migrations

Downstream consumers take `<name>-api` only. The `quarkus-work-api` module is the canonical correct example of this split.

## Why this is non-obvious

The error message says "configure datasource" but the root cause is a transitive dependency bundling entity classes. The module you added was specifically chosen for a non-persistence feature (e.g. a trace ID provider). The natural expectation is that only the entities YOU define affect your persistence unit. There is no warning at dependency declaration time that adding a module will force datasource configuration in your tests.

**See also:** GE-20260423-fce720 "quarkus-work-core FilterRule JPA entity requires a datasource — modules using in-memory persistence fail startup"

**See also:** [GE-20260512-a3838e](GE-20260512-a3838e.md) — transitive hibernate-reactive-panache causes H2 test startup failure

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
quarkus datasource configuration error
"@Entity" class classpath scanning
hibernate orm extension registration

entries.title: quarkus-maven-plugin build goal in extension runtime pom breaks mvn install with datasource error
entries.body:
quarkus-maven-plugin build goal in extension runtime pom breaks mvn install with datasource error

## Symptom

`mvn install` on a Quarkus extension runtime module fails with:

```
Build failure: Build failed due to errors
[error]: Build step HibernateOrmProcessor#configurationDescriptorBuilding threw an exception:
  ConfigurationException: Persistence unit '<default>' defines entities [...] but its datasource
  '<default>' cannot be found: Datasource '<default>' is not configured.
```

No datasource is configured because the runtime module is an extension — not a Quarkus application.

## Context

A `quarkus-maven-plugin` block with `<goal>build</goal>` was added to the extension runtime module's `pom.xml` (typically to enable `@QuarkusTest` support). Extension modules do not build Quarkus applications — they provide build-time and runtime code that other applications consume.

## What was tried (didn't work)

Adding `quarkus.hibernate-orm.enabled=false` to test properties — doesn't help because the `build` goal runs outside the test lifecycle.

## Root cause

The `quarkus-maven-plugin:build` goal triggers a full Quarkus application build, which includes bootstrapping the full extension processor chain including Hibernate ORM. Extension runtime modules have JPA entities (for the extension's own model classes) but no datasource — they rely on the consuming application to provide one. The build goal sees the entities, tries to configure a persistence unit, and fails.

## Fix

Remove the `quarkus-maven-plugin` `<build>` execution block from the extension runtime module's `pom.xml`. The `@QuarkusTest` infrastructure works without it — Quarkus's test framework bootstraps the application through the test lifecycle, not through the `build` goal.

```xml
<!-- Remove this entire block from extension runtime pom.xml -->
<plugin>
  <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
  <artifactId>quarkus-maven-plugin</artifactId>
  <version>${quarkus.version}</version>
  <executions>
    <execution>
      <goals>
        <goal>build</goal>  <!-- WRONG in an extension module -->
      </goals>
    </execution>
  </executions>
</plugin>
```

Keep the `quarkus-extension-maven-plugin` (which generates extension descriptors) — only remove the `quarkus-maven-plugin` with the `build` goal.

## Why this is non-obvious

The `quarkus-maven-plugin` with `build` goal is standard in Quarkus *application* poms. An AI assistant or junior developer adding `@QuarkusTest` support to an extension module may cargo-cult this pattern from application examples. The error message points to a missing datasource, not to the plugin configuration — misdirecting debugging.

## Variant — Library modules (no extension descriptor)

The same failure mode occurs in plain library modules (not Quarkus extensions) that have `quarkus-maven-plugin:build` in their pom — for example, modules that define domain objects or SPIs but have no SPI implementations of their own. The error in this case is a CDI validation failure at build time:

```
[ERROR] Build step io.quarkus.arc.deployment.ArcProcessor#validate threw an exception:
  jakarta.enterprise.inject.spi.DeploymentException: No bean found for required type [...]
```

The module has CDI injection points (from domain classes or interfaces) but no beans to satisfy them — because the implementations live in other modules. CDI validation fires during the `build` goal's full application bootstrap and fails.

**Fix:** Same as above — remove `quarkus-maven-plugin:build` from library modules. These modules are not Quarkus applications; they don't need the build goal. `@QuarkusTest` in downstream modules handles bootstrapping through the test lifecycle.

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
quarkus build goal datasource error
quarkus extension runtime mvn install
hibernate orm configuration exception

entries.title: quarkus-hibernate-reactive-panache in an extension forces Hibernate Reactive to boot for all consumers — @Alternative does not prevent it
entries.body:
quarkus-hibernate-reactive-panache in an extension forces Hibernate Reactive to boot for all consumers — @Alternative does not prevent it

## quarkus-hibernate-reactive-panache in an extension forces Hibernate Reactive to boot for all consumers — @Alternative does not prevent it

**ID:** GE-20260420-dcec35
**Stack:** Quarkus 3.32.2, quarkus-hibernate-reactive-panache

**Symptom:** Adding `quarkus-hibernate-reactive-panache` to a Quarkus extension's runtime `pom.xml` causes `FastBootHibernateReactivePersistenceProvider` to try to initialise on every consumer app startup — even those with no reactive datasource configured. Error: `Unable to find datasource '<default>' for persistence unit '<default>': No pool has been defined`.

Three test classes fail that previously passed: the two using `@TestProfile` (which restart Quarkus) and the one with `@TestTransaction` that triggers JTA coordination with all registered persistence units.

### Root cause
The Hibernate Reactive Panache extension scans for `PanacheRepositoryBase` implementations at **build time** (AOT). Any class implementing the interface — even an `@Alternative` bean — causes the extension to register a reactive persistence unit for the associated entity. `@Alternative` suppresses CDI bean activation but does NOT suppress the build-step registration. At runtime, Hibernate Reactive tries to find a reactive (Vert.x) pool for the registered persistence unit and fails if none is configured.

### Fix
Add to the consumer's test `application.properties`:

```properties
quarkus.datasource.reactive=false
```

This prevents Hibernate Reactive from claiming a reactive pool at runtime, even though the persistence unit was registered at build time.

### Why non-obvious
The error message points to a missing datasource pool — suggesting the fix is to configure a datasource, not to disable reactive. Marking the `PanacheRepositoryBase` bean as `@Alternative` is the obvious CDI workaround and feels correct, but `@Alternative` only controls CDI injection — it has no effect on Quarkus build steps. The fix (`quarkus.datasource.reactive=false`) suppresses the runtime pool lookup entirely, not via CDI.

### Alternatives considered
- `@Alternative` on reactive beans — does not prevent build-step registration; persistence unit still created
- `quarkus.hibernate-reactive.active=false` — property not recognised in Quarkus 3.32.2
- Testcontainers + PostgreSQL — works but adds heavy test infrastructure; unnecessary when H2 suffices

**See also:** GE-20260420-45d53b (fix: quarkus.datasource.reactive=false), GE-20260420-daf5dc (optional dep variant of same issue)

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
quarkus hibernate reactive panache fastboot error
hibernate reactive persistence provider initialization
@Alternative quarkus persistence unit registration

entries.title: quarkus.datasource.reactive=false suppresses Hibernate Reactive boot when extension is on classpath but no reactive pool exists
entries.body:
quarkus.datasource.reactive=false suppresses Hibernate Reactive boot when extension is on classpath but no reactive pool exists

## quarkus.datasource.reactive=false suppresses Hibernate Reactive boot when extension is on classpath but no reactive pool exists

**ID:** GE-20260420-45d53b
**Stack:** Quarkus 3.32.2

**What it does:** Setting `quarkus.datasource.reactive=false` in `application.properties` prevents Hibernate Reactive from attempting to acquire a reactive (Vert.x) connection pool at startup, even when `quarkus-hibernate-reactive-panache` is on the classpath and has registered reactive persistence units at build time.

**Where it works:** Test `application.properties`, per-profile properties, and main `application.properties`.

```properties
# Prevents FastBootHibernateReactivePersistenceProvider from failing
# when no reactive datasource is configured
quarkus.datasource.reactive=false
```

### Why non-obvious
Nothing in the Quarkus extension developer docs mentions this property as a reactive-boot suppressor. The reactive extension activates at build time based on classpath scanning; suppressing it at runtime via a datasource flag is counter-intuitive. The natural search path (Hibernate Reactive docs, `@Alternative`, `quarkus.hibernate-reactive.*` properties) doesn't lead here. Found by trial and error.

**See also:** GE-20260420-33b95f (specific H2+test scenario), GE-20260420-daf5dc (optional dep activation gotcha), GE-20260420-dcec35 (extension forces HR boot even with @Alternative)

entries.title: quarkus-work-core FilterRule JPA entity requires a datasource — modules using in-memory persistence fail startup
entries.body:
quarkus-work-core FilterRule JPA entity requires a datasource — modules using in-memory persistence fail startup

## Symptom

Quarkus startup fails in a module that uses in-memory persistence (no JDBC datasource):

```
ConfigurationException: Datasource '<default>' is not configured.
Persistence unit '<default>' defines entities [io.quarkiverse.work.core.filter.FilterRule],
but its datasource '<default>' cannot be found.
```

## Context

Occurs when `quarkus-work-core` is a transitive dependency (e.g. via `engine` module)
in a Quarkus test module that does not configure a datasource. `FilterRule` is a
`@Entity` (Hibernate ORM Panache) in quarkus-work-core and is discovered by Quarkus's
CDI/Hibernate scanning across all modules on the classpath.

## Root cause

`quarkus-work-core` bundles a `FilterRule` JPA entity and declares Hibernate ORM Panache
as a runtime dependency. Any module that transitively depends on `quarkus-work-core`
inherits the entity scanning, requiring a configured datasource even when the module
has no persistence of its own.

## Fix

Add to the affected module's test `application.properties`:

```properties
# Disable Hibernate ORM so quarkus-work-core's FilterRule entity
# does not require a datasource in modules using in-memory persistence.
quarkus.hibernate-orm.enabled=false
```

## Why this is non-obvious

The module didn't directly depend on `quarkus-work-core` — it arrived as a transitive
dependency through `engine`. The error message names `FilterRule` but gives no indication
of which JAR introduced it or why a datasource is needed in a module that never configured one.

**See also:** GE-20260429-21e6cf "Quarkus: JPA entity in a dependency artifact forces datasource config on ALL downstream consumers"

**See also:** [GE-20260513-74dc72](../casehub-work/GE-20260513-74dc72.md) — casehub-work requires io.casehub.work.runtime.filter in Hibernate scan packages

**See also:** [GE-20260618-08cb96](GE-20260618-08cb96.md) — Named Hibernate ORM PU requires both @PersistenceUnit qualifier AND packages config

entries.title: @QuarkusIntegrationTest must live in a separate module from the extension runtime
entries.body:
@QuarkusIntegrationTest must live in a separate module from the extension runtime

## Symptom

Adding `quarkus-maven-plugin` with the `build` goal to a Quarkus extension runtime module to enable `@QuarkusIntegrationTest` fails at the package phase:

```
ConfigurationException: Datasource '<default>' is not configured.
To solve this, configure datasource '<default>'.
```

The build succeeds in the `test` phase (normal `@QuarkusTest` works fine) but fails in `package` when the plugin tries to produce a deployable artifact.

## Context

Quarkus extensions intentionally omit datasource configuration — consuming applications provide their own. The `quarkus-maven-plugin build` goal performs Quarkus augmentation, which validates that all required configuration is present. Since the extension's `application.properties` has no datasource, augmentation fails.

## What Was Tried

Adding `quarkus-maven-plugin` with build/generate-code/generate-code-tests goals directly to the extension runtime module's `pom.xml`.

## Root Cause

Quarkus augmentation (the build phase) requires a fully configured application. An extension module is not an application — it's a library. The augmentation validation for Hibernate ORM requires a datasource to be present.

## Fix

Create a separate `integration-tests` Maven module that:
1. Depends on the extension runtime (`quarkus-tarkus` etc.)
2. Provides its own `src/main/resources/application.properties` with datasource config (H2 for tests)
3. Contains the `quarkus-maven-plugin` build goal and `maven-failsafe-plugin`
4. Contains `*IT.java` tests annotated `@QuarkusIntegrationTest`

```xml
<!-- integration-tests/pom.xml -->
<dependencies>
  <dependency>
    <groupId>io.quarkiverse.myext</groupId>
    <artifactId>quarkus-myext</artifactId>
    <version>${project.version}</version>
  </dependency>
  <dependency>
    <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
    <artifactId>quarkus-jdbc-h2</artifactId>
  </dependency>
</dependencies>
```

```properties
# integration-tests/src/main/resources/application.properties
quarkus.datasource.db-kind=h2
quarkus.datasource.jdbc.url=jdbc:h2:mem:testdb;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1
quarkus.flyway.migrate-at-start=true
```

## Why This Is Non-Obvious

The `@QuarkusTest` tests in the extension runtime module work perfectly — they start a full Quarkus app including the extension in the same JVM without requiring a packaged artifact. So it seems like `@QuarkusIntegrationTest` should "just work" the same way by adding the plugin. The distinction between "test-phase app boot" and "package-phase augmentation" is not surfaced clearly in the error message.

### Why this fix

The separation keeps the extension module pure (no app-specific config) while enabling native image testing in the integration-tests module where full app configuration is appropriate.

**See also:** GE-0065 — quarkus:dev silently skips if build goal missing; GE-20260417-a405a4 — quarkus-maven-plugin build goal in extension runtime pom breaks mvn install

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
quarkus integration test package failure
quarkus augmentation datasource configuration
@QuarkusIntegrationTest build failure error

entries.title: Quarkus Hibernate ORM schema generation rejects 'create-drop' — correct value is 'drop-and-create'
entries.body:
Quarkus Hibernate ORM schema generation rejects 'create-drop' — correct value is 'drop-and-create'

## What happened

Configuring Hibernate schema generation for test profile based on documentation that uses JPA-standard terminology:

```properties
%test.quarkus.hibernate-orm.database.generation=create-drop
```

Quarkus failed at startup with a config validation error:

```
Cannot convert create-drop to enum class HibernateOrmRuntimeConfigPersistenceUnit$HibernateGenerationStrategy,
allowed values: drop,drop-and-create,create,update,none,validate
```

## Root cause

Quarkus uses its own enum (`HibernateGenerationStrategy`) rather than the JPA-standard `create-drop` value. The Quarkus-specific name is `drop-and-create`. This mismatch is not caught at compile time and only fails at startup.

## Fix

```properties
%test.quarkus.hibernate-orm.database.generation=drop-and-create
```

Allowed values: `drop`, `drop-and-create`, `create`, `update`, `none`, `validate`.

## Why this is non-obvious

JPA standard and Hibernate native both use `create-drop`. External tooling, third-party docs, and AI assistants often suggest `create-drop` because it is the standard JPA term. Quarkus silently diverges without aliasing the standard value.

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
Quarkus HibernateGenerationStrategy enum
Quarkus config validation error create-drop
Quarkus test profile hibernate-orm schema generation

entries.title: Named Hibernate ORM persistence unit requires both @PersistenceUnit qualifier AND packages config for entity discovery
entries.body:
Named Hibernate ORM persistence unit requires both @PersistenceUnit qualifier AND packages config for entity discovery

### Symptom

JPA queries return empty results or `em.find()` returns null for entities that exist in the database. No error, no warning — Hibernate simply doesn't see the entity class.

### Context

Adding a JPA entity to an application that shares a foundation module's named persistence unit (e.g. Qhorus's `qhorus` PU). The entity is in a different package than the foundation module's entities.

### Root cause

Two independent configuration points must both be set:

1. `@PersistenceUnit("qhorus")` on the EntityManager injection — without it, the default PU is used, which has no datasource configured
2. `quarkus.hibernate-orm.qhorus.packages` must include the new entity's package — Hibernate only scans packages listed in this config for the named PU

Missing either one causes silent failure. The compound nature is what makes this non-obvious — setting only the annotation or only the packages config both appear correct in isolation but produce empty results.

### Fix

Both changes are required:

```java
@Inject
@PersistenceUnit("qhorus")
EntityManager em;
```

```properties
# application.properties — extend the existing packages list
quarkus.hibernate-orm.qhorus.packages=io.casehub.qhorus.runtime,io.casehub.ledger.runtime,io.casehub.drafthouse
```

### Why this is non-obvious

Each configuration point has its own diagnostic blind spot:
- Missing `@PersistenceUnit`: the default PU has no datasource, so Quarkus may fail at startup with an opaque CDI error OR silently use a different (empty) schema
- Missing packages config: the entity class exists on the classpath and the PU is correct, but Hibernate's entity scan doesn't find it — no warning, just empty results
- Both missing: you get the compound failure of both above

Related entries cover individual aspects — GE-20260422-334eb8 covers the annotation import (`io.quarkus.hibernate.orm.PersistenceUnit` not `jakarta.persistence.PersistenceUnit`), GE-20260424-6b88a0 covers datasource routing. This entry covers the compound requirement.

**See also:** [GE-20260612-8e925b](GE-20260612-8e925b.md) — Quarkus quarkus.hibernate-orm.<pu-name>.sql-load-script for named PU | [GE-20260512-ea776c](GE-20260512-ea776c.md) — Quarkus named persistence units silently skip schema generation | [GE-20260521-2b82e7](GE-20260521-2b82e7.md) — Panache.withTransaction() uses the default persistence unit | [GE-20260530-da427e](GE-20260530-da427e.md) — Quarkus multi-PU sub-package matching assigns entities to wrong PU | [GE-20260423-fce720](GE-20260423-fce720.md) — quarkus-work-core FilterRule JPA entity requires datasource | [GE-20260429-21e6cf](GE-20260429-21e6cf.md) — JPA entity in dependency forces datasource config on all downstream consumers

entries.title: Hibernate 6 SessionFactoryObserverForNamedQueryValidation throws at boot for schema-drifted JARs — quarkus property overrides don't suppress it
entries.body:
Hibernate 6 SessionFactoryObserverForNamedQueryValidation throws at boot for schema-drifted JARs — quarkus property overrides don't suppress it

## Symptom

`@QuarkusTest` fails at boot with:

```
jakarta.persistence.PersistenceException: Unable to build Hibernate SessionFactory
Caused by: org.hibernate.query.NamedQueryValidationException: Errors in named queries:
  Suppressed: org.hibernate.query.sqm.UnknownPathException:
    Could not resolve attribute 'scopeKey' of 'io.casehub.ledger.runtime.model.ActorTrustScore'
```

The error also appears as `ERROR` log lines before the exception:
```
HHH90003001: Error in named query: ActorTrustScore.findGlobalByActorId:
  org.hibernate.query.sqm.UnknownPathException: Could not resolve attribute 'scopeKey'
```

Hibernate throws this at `sessionFactoryCreated()` time — before any test runs.

## Root Cause

A cached `casehub-ledger:0.2-SNAPSHOT` JAR contains `@NamedQuery` annotations on `ActorTrustScore` that reference a field (`scopeKey`) not yet present on the entity class. This happens when the `@NamedQuery` strings were committed to the repo but the corresponding entity field wasn't added yet (or vice versa), and the local Maven cache holds a stale artifact version.

Hibernate 6 validates ALL named queries at `SessionFactory` build time via `SessionFactoryObserverForNamedQueryValidation` — a Quarkus Hibernate ORM extension class. Unlike Hibernate 5, there is no documented configuration key to skip this validation.

**Attempts that don't work:**
- `quarkus.hibernate-orm.validate-named-query=false` — not a valid Quarkus config key
- `quarkus.hibernate-orm.unsupported-properties."hibernate.query.validate_named_queries"=false` — also ineffective; the Quarkus observer runs after Hibernate's own validation hooks

## Fix

Install the affected artifact from local source:

```bash
mvn install -DskipTests -q --batch-mode -f /path/to/ledger/pom.xml
```

This overwrites the stale SNAPSHOT JAR in `~/.m2/` with a consistent version where named queries and entity fields match.

If local source is unavailable, force Maven to re-download the SNAPSHOT:
```bash
mvn dependency:resolve -U  # -U forces SNAPSHOT refresh
```

## Why This Is Non-Obvious

1. The error log says `HHH90003001` and mentions a named query — nothing suggests the problem is a stale JAR artifact. A developer investigates entity mappings, not Maven cache consistency.
2. The entity class on disk is correct; the problem is inside the compiled JAR from cache. Reading source code shows no issue.
3. The two Quarkus/Hibernate property overrides that should disable validation are both silently ignored — the validation happens in a Quarkus extension observer, not in Hibernate's standard configuration layer.
4. Tests pass on CI (which always downloads fresh artifacts) but fail locally on cached SNAPSHOTs — intermittent environment-specific failure with no clear signal.

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
`jakarta.persistence.PersistenceException` `ActorTrustScore`
`SessionFactoryObserverForNamedQueryValidation` `NamedQueryValidationException`
`hibernate.query.sqm.UnknownPathException` `scopeKey`

entries.title: quarkus-hibernate-reactive-panache as <optional>true</optional> dep still activates Hibernate Reactive extension in the module's own tests
entries.body:
quarkus-hibernate-reactive-panache as <optional>true</optional> dep still activates Hibernate Reactive extension in the module's own tests

## Symptom

Adding `quarkus-hibernate-reactive-panache` with `<optional>true</optional>` to `pom.xml` causes `@QuarkusTest` tests to fail with:

```
ConfigurationException: Unable to find datasource '<default>' for persistence unit '<default>':
No pool has been defined for persistence unit <default>
```

Tests that were passing before now fail to start the Quarkus application.

## Context

Occurs when:
1. A library/extension module adds `quarkus-hibernate-reactive-panache` as an optional dep (to support reactive consumers without forcing the dep on everyone)
2. The same module has `@QuarkusTest` integration tests using H2 JDBC

## Root Cause

Maven `<optional>true</optional>` prevents the dep from being transitively propagated to downstream consumers — but it does **not** remove the dep from the current module's own test classpath. The dep is still fully present during `mvn test`.

With the reactive Panache extension on the classpath, Quarkus's build-time bootstrap activates the Hibernate Reactive extension. That extension requires a Vert.x reactive datasource — not a JDBC pool. H2 has no Vert.x reactive driver, so no pool can be created and Quarkus fails to start.

`quarkus.arc.exclude-types` does NOT fix this — it only affects CDI bean scan, not Quarkus extension activation.

## Fix

Remove `quarkus-hibernate-reactive-panache` from the module's `pom.xml` entirely. Provide only the SPI interface (which only needs `io.smallrye.mutiny.Uni`, already on the Quarkus classpath). Consumers who want reactive add the dep to their own module.

```xml
<!-- DON'T add this to a module with @QuarkusTest using H2 -->
<!-- <dependency>
  <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
  <artifactId>quarkus-hibernate-reactive-panache</artifactId>
  <optional>true</optional>
</dependency> -->
```

If a pre-built reactive implementation is needed, put it in a **separate Maven module** (e.g. `quarkus-mylib-reactive`) so the reactive dep never lands on the blocking test classpath.

## Why This Is Non-Obvious

The Maven `optional` flag is commonly understood to mean "this dep won't bother consumers" — developers assume it also means "won't cause problems in my own tests." The Quarkus extension activation is a build-time concern triggered by classpath presence, not by CDI bean wiring or config. The error message (`No pool has been defined for persistence unit <default>`) doesn't mention reactive or optional dependencies at all.

**See also:** GE-20260420-33b95f (fix: %test.quarkus.datasource.reactive=false), GE-20260420-45d53b (general mechanism), GE-20260420-dcec35 (extension-level variant)

**See also:** GE-20260420-cbd0fa (H2 cannot be used as reactive datasource, vertx-jdbc-client not enough)

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
quarkus hibernate reactive panache test failure
quarkus optional dep test error
hibernate reactive datasource h2

entries.title: Panache entities cannot be scanned by two Quarkus persistence units simultaneously
entries.body:
Panache entities cannot be scanned by two Quarkus persistence units simultaneously

### Symptom

Build-time `IllegalStateException: Panache entities do not support being attached to several persistence units: io.example.MyEntity is attached to: <default>,qhorus`

### Context

Quarkus project with two named persistence units configured via `quarkus.hibernate-orm.packages` and `quarkus.hibernate-orm.qhorus.packages`. Occurs when the same Java package appears in both lists — even if you intended only a subset of entities in that package to be managed by the second PU.

### What was tried

Added a `LedgerEntry` subclass to `io.casehub.clinical.entity` (alongside regular Panache entities), then listed `io.casehub.clinical.entity` in both `hibernate-orm.packages` and `hibernate-orm.qhorus.packages` so both entity types would be visible to their respective PUs.

### Root cause

Quarkus scans the entire package for all entity classes when a package is listed in a PU's `packages` config. Panache entities found in both scans are flagged as "belonging to two PUs" at build time — Panache's proxy mechanism cannot support this.

### Fix

Put JPA entities managed by the second PU in a **separate package** not listed under the default PU:

```properties
# Default PU — Panache entities only
quarkus.hibernate-orm.packages=io.casehub.clinical.entity

# Second PU — separate package for non-Panache JPA entities
quarkus.hibernate-orm.qhorus.packages=io.casehub.ledger.runtime.model,io.casehub.clinical.ledger
```

Create the new package (`io.casehub.clinical.ledger` or similar) and place the non-Panache JPA entities there.

### Why this is non-obvious

The natural instinct is to put a new entity subclass alongside related entities. The error appears at build time (not runtime), but the message doesn't explain that the fix requires a separate package — it just says the entity is "attached to" two PUs.

**See also:** [GE-20260423-4aa1e0](GE-20260423-4aa1e0.md) — JPA InheritanceType.JOINED forces all hierarchy entities into one persistence unit

**See also:** [GE-20260422-334eb8](GE-20260422-334eb8.md) — Quarkus named persistence unit EntityManager injection uses io.quarkus.hibernate.orm.PersistenceUnit qualifier

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
`IllegalStateException Panache entity attached to multiple persistence units`
`quarkus hibernate-orm packages qhorus entity conflict`
`Panache proxy mechanism multiple persistence units`

entries.title: casehub-qhorus activates quarkus-hibernate-reactive unconditionally — fails with JDBC H2 at startup
entries.body:
casehub-qhorus activates quarkus-hibernate-reactive unconditionally — fails with JDBC H2 at startup

## Symptom

Quarkus fails at startup with an error about a reactive Vert.x pool or reactive datasource not being configured, even though the application only uses JDBC H2 and `casehub.qhorus.reactive.enabled=false` is set.

```
Failed to start quarkus: Reactive datasource 'qhorus' requires a reactive driver
io.quarkus.runtime.QuarkusBindException: ...Vert.x pool...
```

## Context

Any Quarkus application that adds `casehub-qhorus` as a Maven dependency will trigger this failure if it does not provide a reactive datasource. The `casehub.qhorus.reactive.enabled=false` build-time flag exists in qhorus but does **not** suppress the Quarkus hibernate-reactive extension from activating — it only controls qhorus's own reactive messaging layer.

## Root Cause

`casehub-qhorus` has a compile-scope dependency on `quarkus-hibernate-reactive-panache`. When the deployment JAR of that extension is on the classpath, Quarkus activates the reactive persistence layer unconditionally at augmentation time — before any `@IfBuildProperty` guards in qhorus's own processors can suppress it. The result is that Quarkus tries to create a reactive Vert.x pool for every configured datasource, including the default H2 JDBC datasource, which has no reactive driver.

## Fix

Add these properties to `application.properties` (or `src/test/resources/application.properties` for tests):

```properties
# Suppress reactive datasource activation — casehub-qhorus pulls in
# quarkus-hibernate-reactive-panache unconditionally; this prevents Quarkus
# from trying to wire a reactive Vert.x pool to JDBC datasources.
quarkus.datasource.reactive=false
quarkus.datasource.qhorus.reactive=false
```

**Do NOT add `casehub.qhorus.reactive.enabled=false`** — this key was removed from the qhorus config model in a later 0.2-SNAPSHOT build. Adding it now causes `ConfigValidationException` at startup, a hard failure with a misleading error message. The two standard Quarkus properties above are sufficient.

## ⚠️ Deprecated property (added 2026-05-17)

`casehub.qhorus.reactive.enabled=false` was a valid workaround in earlier qhorus 0.2-SNAPSHOT builds but was **removed from the qhorus config model** by qhorus 0.2-SNAPSHOT (circa 2026-05). Adding it to `application.properties` now causes:

```
io.smallrye.config.ConfigValidationException: SRCFG00014: The config property casehub.qhorus.reactive.enabled
with the config value 'false' was converted to null from the converter
```

This is a hard startup failure with a misleading error — it looks like a config parsing problem, not a stale property name. Remove this key from any application.properties file where it was previously added.

## Why This Is Non-Obvious

The error message says "reactive datasource not configured" — pointing at the datasource config, not at qhorus. A developer troubleshooting this naturally adds reactive datasource config rather than suppressing reactive entirely. The qhorus build-time flag (`casehub.qhorus.reactive.enabled`) sounds like it should solve the problem, but it operates at the application layer, not the Quarkus augmentation layer.

### Why this fix

Setting `quarkus.datasource.reactive=false` is the correct Quarkus mechanism to suppress reactive pool creation per datasource. The two-property combination is required because qhorus uses a named datasource (`qhorus`) in addition to the default — both must be suppressed independently.

## Structural Fix

Protocol PP-20260514-f41258 prescribes the correct extension-level fix:
mark `quarkus-hibernate-reactive-panache` as `<optional>true</optional>` in the
runtime pom; in the deployment processor replace the config flag with
`Capabilities.isPresent(Capability.HIBERNATE_REACTIVE)` as the BooleanSupplier;
produce `ExcludedTypeBuildItem` for reactive classes when capability is absent and
for blocking counterparts when it is present. Classpath presence becomes the single
source of truth — no consumer-side suppression needed.

Tracked as casehub-qhorus#141. Once that ships:
- The two-property workaround is obsolete
- Remove reactive suppression from: claudony app/test, devtown app/test, aml app/test, clinical app/test

**See also:** [GE-20260420-cbd0fa](../quarkus/GE-20260420-cbd0fa.md) — Quarkus Hibernate Reactive @QuarkusTest cannot use H2

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
quarkus hibernate-reactive reactive datasource error
casehub-qhorus reactive activation quarkus
quarkus bind exception reactive vertx pool

entries.title: Quarkus Hibernate Reactive @QuarkusTest cannot use H2 — vertx-jdbc-client alone doesn't register the reactive pool factory
entries.body:
Quarkus Hibernate Reactive @QuarkusTest cannot use H2 — vertx-jdbc-client alone doesn't register the reactive pool factory

## Symptom

`@QuarkusTest` with `quarkus.datasource.reactive=true` (set via `@TestProfile`) and `vertx-jdbc-client` on the classpath fails at context startup:

```
No reactive datasource configured
```

or the reactive Hibernate session is never initialised and all `@RunOnVertxContext` tests are skipped/fail. Adding `quarkus.datasource.reactive.url=h2:mem:...` doesn't help.

## Root Cause

Quarkus's reactive pool factory is only registered by **native reactive client Quarkus extensions** — `quarkus-reactive-pg-client`, `quarkus-reactive-mysql-client`, etc. The raw `vertx-jdbc-client` jar is a JDBC bridge, but Quarkus does not wire it as a managed reactive datasource. H2 has no native async driver; there is no Quarkus reactive H2 extension.

## Fix

For reactive Hibernate Panache integration tests, use PostgreSQL with Docker:

1. Add `quarkus-reactive-pg-client` as a test dependency
2. Enable Dev Services (requires Docker): Quarkus auto-starts a PostgreSQL container
3. Set `quarkus.datasource.reactive=true` and `quarkus.datasource.db-kind=postgresql` in the test profile

If Docker is unavailable, write the reactive JPA tests as `@Disabled` with an explanatory comment. Unit tests via `InMemoryReactive*Store` (direct instantiation, `.await().indefinitely()`) still work without any datasource.

## Why This Is Non-Obvious

`vertx-jdbc-client` is described as a JDBC bridge that enables reactive-style access over blocking JDBC drivers. It's reasonable to assume adding it to the classpath would enable reactive H2. The Quarkus docs don't document this limitation explicitly — the reactive datasource section discusses PostgreSQL, MySQL, and MariaDB but doesn't mention that other drivers simply won't work regardless of the JDBC bridge.

**See also:** GE-20260416-f02f95 (VertxContextSupport.subscribeAndAwait() for reactive Panache in tests), GE-20260420-33b95f (H2 + hibernate-reactive classpath fix)

**See also:** GE-20260420-daf5dc (optional dep still activates Hibernate Reactive extension)

**See also:** [GE-20260508-492336](../casehub-qhorus/GE-20260508-492336.md) — casehub-qhorus activates quarkus-hibernate-reactive unconditionally, fails with JDBC H2

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---

entries.title: Quarkus schema-management.strategy is build-time — QuarkusTestProfile.getConfigOverrides() cannot change it
entries.body:
Quarkus schema-management.strategy is build-time — QuarkusTestProfile.getConfigOverrides() cannot change it

### Symptom

`QuarkusTestProfile.getConfigOverrides()` sets `quarkus.hibernate-orm.<pu>.schema-management.strategy=none` but Hibernate still runs `drop-and-create` (from the `%test.` application.properties value).

### Context

Named persistence unit (`qhorus`) with `%test.quarkus.hibernate-orm.qhorus.schema-management.strategy=drop-and-create` in test `application.properties`. A test profile tries to override this to `none` so Flyway manages the schema instead. The override appears in SmallRye Config but Hibernate ignores it.

### Root cause

`schema-management.strategy` (formerly `database.generation`) is processed during Quarkus augmentation (build phase). `getConfigOverrides()` applies at runtime — after the augmentation has already decided the schema action. The build-time `%test.` value wins.

### Fix

Do not rely on `getConfigOverrides()` to change `schema-management.strategy`. Set the desired value directly in the `%test.` application.properties (build-time config). If different test classes need different strategies, use Flyway for all tests and control schema creation through migration locations.

### Why this is non-obvious

The Quarkus docs classify `schema-management.strategy` as "overridable at runtime" and `getConfigOverrides()` is the standard mechanism for per-test-class config. The override shows no warning, no error, and appears in config dumps. The only signal is that Hibernate's DDL still runs — which looks like a Hibernate bug, not a config precedence issue.

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
Quarkus Hibernate schema-management strategy override
QuarkusTestProfile getConfigOverrides none
Hibernate drop-and-create schema management

entries.title: quarkus.mcp.server.tools.page-size controls tools/list pagination — undocumented default of 50 silently truncates large tool sets
entries.body:
quarkus.mcp.server.tools.page-size controls tools/list pagination — undocumented default of 50 silently truncates large tool sets

## `quarkus.mcp.server.tools.page-size` controls tools/list pagination — undocumented default of 50 silently truncates large tool sets

### Stack
quarkus-mcp-server 1.11.1 (Quarkiverse)

### What it is
`quarkus.mcp.server.tools.page-size` is a runtime configuration property in quarkus-mcp-server that controls how many tools are returned per `tools/list` MCP response. It is defined in `McpServerRuntimeConfig.java` as a nested interface:

```java
public interface Tools {
    @WithDefault("50")
    int pageSize();
    // ...
}
```

### How to use it

**Disable pagination** (return all tools in one response):
```properties
quarkus.mcp.server.tools.page-size=0
```

**Set a custom page size:**
```properties
quarkus.mcp.server.tools.page-size=100
```

Setting to 0 or any negative number disables pagination entirely — all registered tools are returned in a single `tools/list` response regardless of count.

### Where it's not documented
As of quarkus-mcp-server 1.11.1, this property does not appear in the main Quarkiverse documentation for the extension. It is only discoverable by:
- Reading the `McpServerRuntimeConfig.java` source
- Noticing that `tools/list` returns fewer tools than expected (no warning is emitted)
- Decompiling the deployment JAR

### Discovery path
Found by: diagnosing silent tool truncation (49 Qhorus + 8 Claudony = 57 total tools, response showing exactly 50 alphabetically-sorted tools). Traced through `ToolMessageHandler` → `fetchPage()` → `serverConfig.tools().pageSize()` → `@WithDefault("50")` in `McpServerRuntimeConfig`.

### Related config
The same nested config likely controls pagination for other MCP feature types (prompts, resources) via similar `pageSize()` methods. The naming convention is `quarkus.mcp.server.<feature-type>.page-size`.

**See also:** GE-20260501-50a9f4 — quarkus-mcp-server silently caps tools/list at 50 | GE-20260414-fa6489 — @ToolArg undocumented required and defaultValue attributes

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
quarkus mcp server page size default
mcp server tools list pagination pageSize

entries.title: GitHub Packages REST API silently truncates org package listing — no pagination indicator
entries.body:
GitHub Packages REST API silently truncates org package listing — no pagination indicator

### Symptom
`gh api 'orgs/{org}/packages?package_type=maven'` returns a subset of packages.
Packages known to exist and be published do not appear in the results. No error,
no warning, no indication that results are truncated.

### Context
Auditing whether all Maven modules in a multi-repo build are published to GitHub
Packages. The org has 200+ packages. Default page size is 30.

### What was tried (didn't work)
- Single API call to list all packages — returned only ~30, missing entire repos
- Assumed packages were not published and began investigating CI workflows

### Root cause
The GitHub REST API `/orgs/{org}/packages` endpoint paginates at 30 items by
default. Unlike most GitHub API endpoints, the `gh` CLI does not auto-paginate
this one. There is no `total_count` field or obvious truncation marker in the
response — the caller gets a valid JSON array that simply stops early.

### Fix
Use `per_page=100` and iterate pages until an empty page is returned:
```bash
# Page through all packages
gh api 'orgs/{org}/packages?package_type=maven&per_page=100&page=1' --jq '.[].name'
gh api 'orgs/{org}/packages?package_type=maven&per_page=100&page=2' --jq '.[].name'
# ... until empty result
```

Or check specific packages by name (O(1), no pagination):
```bash
gh api 'orgs/{org}/packages/maven/{groupId}.{artifactId}/versions' \
  --jq '.[0].name' 2>/dev/null || echo "NOT FOUND"
```

### Why this is non-obvious
Most GitHub API endpoints either return all results or include clear pagination
indicators (Link headers, total_count). This endpoint silently returns a partial
list. The natural debugging path is to investigate CI/CD publishing, not API
pagination — especially when the first page contains packages from other repos
in the org, making the response look complete.

### Why this fix
Checking specific packages by name avoids pagination entirely and is O(1) per
package. Use the paginated listing only when you need the full inventory.

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
`gh api 'orgs/{org}/packages?package_type=maven'` pagination
`org packages api truncation`
`github packages per_page 100`

WEIGHTED_MAJORITY attestation aggregation silently masks contradicting verdicts on the same entry
entries.body:
WEIGHTED_MAJORITY attestation aggregation silently masks contradicting verdicts on the same entry

### Symptom
Capability trust scores remain unchanged (e.g. 11/12 = 0.917) regardless of how many FLAGGED attestations are written against an actor's decisions. Investigation naturally targets the query layer, computation logic, or score persistence — all of which are correct.

### Context
Bayesian Beta trust scoring with a four-pass pipeline (capability → dimension → cap×dim → global). Attestations are aggregated per (entryId, capabilityTag) group before scoring. An incident feedback system writes a FLAGGED attestation against an existing entry that already holds a SOUND attestation from the original review.

### What was tried (didn't work)
- Checked query layer (findAllEvents, findAttestationsForEntries) — fetches all verdicts correctly
- Checked TrustScoreComputer.compute() — handles FLAGGED by incrementing beta correctly
- Checked PerActorTrustComputer delegation — passes data through unchanged
- Checked JPA upsert — updates existing score rows correctly
- Checked TrustScoreSource/TrustGateService — reads directly from repository
- All unit tests with FLAGGED on separate entries pass

### Root cause
`TrustScoreCalculator.computeAll()` runs `buildEffectiveAttestations()` which groups attestations by (entryId, capabilityTag) and aggregates via `AttestationAggregator.weightedMajority()`. When an entry has SOUND(confidence=1.0) + FLAGGED(confidence=0.9):
- positive = 1.0, negative = 0.9
- `positive >= negative` → verdict = SOUND
- confidence = |1.0 - 0.9| / 1.9 ≈ 0.053
- Weight in compute() = decayWeight × 0.053 ≈ 0 → neither alpha nor beta increment meaningfully

The FLAGGED attestation is not ignored — it is aggregated into a near-zero-weight SOUND, which is worse: it cancels the original SOUND's contribution too.

### Fix
Use raw attestations (not aggregated) for the capability pass. Each individual attestation contributes to alpha/beta independently — SOUND increments alpha, FLAGGED increments beta, both on the same entry. The dimension pass already used raw attestations; this brings the capability pass into alignment.

```java
// Before (broken): used effectiveAttestations (pre-aggregated)
final Map<String, Map<UUID, List<LedgerAttestation>>> byCapabilityAndEntry =
        effectiveAttestations.stream()
                .filter(a -> !CapabilityTag.GLOBAL.equals(a.capabilityTag))
                ...

// After (fixed): uses rawAttestations
final Map<String, Map<UUID, List<LedgerAttestation>>> byCapabilityAndEntry =
        rawAttestations.stream()
                .filter(a -> a.capabilityTag != null
                        && !CapabilityTag.GLOBAL.equals(a.capabilityTag))
                ...
```

Note the added null guard on `capabilityTag` — raw attestations don't pass through `buildEffectiveAttestations` which normalizes nulls to GLOBAL.

### Why this is non-obvious
The aggregation step sits between data fetch and computation. Both endpoints work correctly in isolation. The symptom (score unchanged) points at the computation or query layer. The aggregation is designed to reduce noise from multiple attestors — it silently converts the sequential-evidence case (SOUND then FLAGGED over time) into the concurrent-vote case (competing opinions) without any log message or signal.

### Why this fix
Raw attestations are the right model for capability scoring because attestations on the same entry arrive at different times as sequential evidence (review outcome, then incident feedback), not as concurrent competing votes. The aggregation model was designed for the N-attestors-same-time case. Trade-off: N attestors on the same entry now contribute N× weight instead of 1× consensus weight — an idea has been logged to explore a hybrid approach.

### Alternatives considered
- Changing the WEIGHTED_MAJORITY tie-break from `>=` to `>` — still produces SOUND for the 1.0 vs 0.9 case; doesn't fix the core issue
- Adding a temporal-awareness flag to the aggregator — overengineered for the current use case; the raw-attestation approach is simpler and matches the dimension pass
- Processing attestations individually with no aggregation anywhere — would affect the global pass which intentionally uses aggregation via GlobalScoreStrategy SPI

---HYPOTHETICAL-QUERIES---
findAllEvents FLAGGED attestation
TrustScoreComputer compute() SOUND verdict
weightedMajority attestation aggregation
